<issue identifier="MM-457">
<title>Phase 2: Foreign-PDS session provider — password `createSession` unlock path for non-Custos hosts</title>
<description>
Part of <issue id="d5cb6e3d-f781-4ecb-aebf-c954915b3708" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-452/obsign-without-custos-first-class-any-pds-wallet-support-epic">MM-452</issue>. Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` §Phase 2.

## What

Several wallet features are built entirely on standard lexicons but are dark for foreign-hosted identities only because the session that drives them comes from Custos's `/v1/sessions/sovereign`:

* App passwords (`createAppPassword`/`listAppPasswords`/`revokeAppPassword`)
* Change handle (`updateHandle` + the wallet-signed alsoKnownAs op)
* Identity removal (`requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` + tombstone)
* **Blob restore** (`restore_blob_backup`'s `uploadBlob` leg — backup works everywhere, restore doesn't)

`SessionProvider::full_access_client`'s `NeedsUnlock` currently has exactly one resolution: the biometric passwordless `sovereignLogin`. Give it a second: on hosts without the `sovereignSessions` capability (<issue id="e2abaa52-2747-4daf-8c10-209294bd5183" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-454/phase-0b-custos-capability-extension-in-describeserver-self">MM-454</issue>), the unlock cue routes to a password `createSession` prompt (the machinery `source_login.rs` already uses transiently for claim/migration source login), persisting the resulting Bearer pair in the same versioned `{did}:oauth-tokens` record so refresh/rotation flows through the provider's existing ladder unchanged.

## Constraints

* ADR-0021 holds: identity ops need a full session; hosts may email-2FA (`AuthFactorTokenRequired` is already modeled in `PdsClient::create_session`).
* The password is used once and never stored — identical posture to the claim flow.
* Per-feature graceful degradation stays honest: a host that refuses an operation (e.g. no app-password support) surfaces the server's answer, not a wallet guess.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A claimed [bsky.social/reference-PDS](<http://bsky.social/reference-PDS>) identity can mint, list, and revoke app passwords; change handle; run account removal; and restore its blob backup — each behind the same biometric gates as the Custos paths.
2. `SessionError::NeedsUnlock` handling in the frontend branches on host capability: sovereign login (Custos) vs password prompt (other), with 2FA handled.
3. Refresh, host-change discard, and coalescing behavior of `session_provider.rs` are unchanged for Custos identities (existing tests stay green).
</description>

<id>d5cb6e3d-f781-4ecb-aebf-c954915b3708</id>
<title>Obsign without Custos — first-class any-PDS wallet support (epic)</title>
<description>
## Strategy

Broaden Obsign's market beyond Custos-hosted accounts: a user on the reference PDS, [bsky.social](<http://bsky.social>), or any spec-compliant PDS should get real, honest value from the wallet — Secure-Enclave root key, PLC monitoring + 72h override, user-held repo/media backup, self-held Shamir recovery — with Custos capabilities (escrow-assisted recovery, passwordless sovereign sessions, agents, wallet-confirmed consent) as the opt-in upgrade rather than a lock-in. Rescue and migration must never force a stressed user onto Custos.

Design doc: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` (survey of what already works without Custos, the ecosystem describeServer survey, the capability-extension design, and phase rationale).

## As-built starting point (verified 2026-07-24, v0.8.1)

Already works on any PDS today: the claim/import flow (device key → `rotationKeys[0]` via standard lexicons), PLC monitoring + recovery override ([plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) only), repo + blob backup (public sync endpoints, no session), endpoint repair, sovereign share-based recovery (Shares 1+3), and disaster recovery **into a Custos destination**.

Custos-locked today: create ceremony, Shamir generation/re-key (fused to `/v1/dids` + escrow), sovereign sessions (and everything downstream: app passwords, change handle, removal, blob restore), agents/consent, and the rescue/migration **destination** (finalize unconditionally mints `/v1/sessions/sovereign`).

## Phases (one child issue each)

* Phase 0a — mode-select honesty: "Create an identity" / "Import an identity" + non-Custos create gate
* Phase 0b — `custos` capability extension in describeServer + self-identifying `_health`
* Phase 0c — positioning + live validation of the any-PDS arc (claim → backup → rescue)
* Phase 1 — self-held Shamir kit for foreign-hosted identities (escrow-less re-key)
* Phase 2 — foreign-PDS session provider (password `createSession` unlock path)
* Phase 3 — any-PDS rescue/migration destination (capability-gated finalize)

Parked (needs its own design pass, deliberately not in this epic): "create-then-sovereignize" — creating a brand-new account on a reference PDS via standard `createAccount` then immediately running the claim ceremony.
</description>
</parent-issue>

<issue-ref identifier="MM-458" title="Phase 3: Any-PDS rescue and migration destination — capability-gated finalize"/>
</related>
</issue-relations>
</issue>

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. - ed3d-plan-and-execute:code-reviewer: Reviews completed project steps against plans and enforces coding standards. Blocks merges for Minor, Important, or Critical issues. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:task-implementor-fast: Implements individual tasks from plans with TDD, skill application, verification, and git commits. Use when executing a specific task that requires writing, modifying, or testing code as part of a larger plan. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-plan-and-execute:test-analyst: Use after final code review passes to validate test coverage against acceptance criteria and generate human test plans - reads test-requirements.md, verifies automated tests exist, produces manual verification documentation (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-playwright:playwright-explorer: Use when exploring websites, proving hypotheses about web application behavior, automating browser interactions, or generating E2E tests - investigates page structure through accessibility snapshots, tests assumptions systematically, and coordinates Playwright MCP tools with tenacity to complete complex multi-step investigations (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:codebase-investigator: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need to understand current codebase state, find existing patterns, or verify assumptions about what exists. Examples: <example>Context: Starting brainstorming phase and need to understand current authentication implementation. user: "I want to add OAuth support to our app" assistant: "Let me use the codebase-investigator agent to understand how authentication currently works before we design the OAuth integration" <commentary>Before designing new features, investigate existing patterns to ensure the design builds on what's already there.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Writing implementation plan and need to verify file locations and current structure. user: "Create a plan for adding user profiles" assistant: "I'll use the codebase-investigator agent to verify the current user model structure and find where user-related code lives" <commentary>Investigation prevents hallucinating file paths or assuming structure that doesn't exist.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:combined-researcher: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need current information BOTH the local system AND from the internet, API documentation, library usage patterns, or external knowledge. Examples: <example>Context: Designing integration with external service and need to understand current API. user: "I want to integrate with the Stripe API for payments" assistant: "Let me use the combined-researcher agent to find if and how we currently use Stripe, and then the current Stripe API documentation and best practices for integration" <commentary>Before designing integrations, research current API state and current local codebase state to ensure plan matches reality.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Evaluating technology choices for implementation plan. user: "Should we use library X or Y for this feature?" assistant: "I'll use the combined-researcher agent to research what we've currently selected already, then if we haven't selected something we'll look at both libraries' current status, features, and community recommendations" <commentary>Research helps make informed technology decisions based on current information.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:internet-researcher: Use this agent when planning or designing features and you need current information from the internet, API documentation, library usage patterns, or external knowledge. Examples: <example>Context: Designing integration with external service and need to understand current API. user: "I want to integrate with the Stripe API for payments" assistant: "Let me use the internet-researcher agent to find the current Stripe API documentation and best practices for integration" <commentary>Before designing integrations, research current API state to ensure plan matches reality.</commentary></example> <example>Context: Evaluating technology choices for implementation plan. user: "Should we use library X or Y for this feature?" assistant: "I'll use the internet-researcher agent to research both libraries' current status, features, and community recommendations" <commentary>Research helps make informed technology decisions based on current information.</commentary></example> (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-research-agents:remote-code-researcher: Use when understanding how external libraries or open-source projects implement features by examining actual source code - finds repos via web search, clones to a stable cache directory, investigates with codebase analysis. Triggers: "how does library X implement Y", "show me how Z handles this", "I want to see the actual code for", evaluating library internals before adoption. (Tools: All tools except Agent)

- ed3d-session-reflection:conversation-reviewer: Use when reviewing a Claude Code session transcript for quality — analyzes human prompting effectiveness, agent performance patterns, and environment/tooling gaps, then writes structured findings to a specified output file. Requires a reduced transcript path and output path. (Tools: Read, Write, Bash, Grep, Glob, Skill)

- episodic-memory:search-conversations: Gives you memory across sessions. You don't automatically remember past conversations - THIS AGENT RESTORES IT. Search your history before starting any task to recover decisions, solutions, and lessons learned. (Tools: Read, mcp__plugin_episodic-memory_episodic-memory__search, mcp__plugin_episodic-memory_episodic-memory__show)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by doing a git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent.

<function call omitted for brevity>
assistant: "Now I'll use the Task tool to launch the code-reviewer agent to review this implementation."
<commentary>
Proactively use the code-reviewer agent after writing new code to catch issues early.
</commentary>

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/linear-workflow

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

{"id":"MM-457","title":"Phase 2: Foreign-PDS session provider — password `createSession` unlock path for non-Custos hosts","description":"Part of <issue id="d5cb6e3d-f781-4ecb-aebf-c954915b3708" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-452/obsign-without-custos-first-class-any-pds-wallet-support-epic">MM-452</issue>. Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` §Phase 2.

## What

Several wallet features are built entirely on standard lexicons but are dark for foreign-hosted identities only because the session that drives them comes from Custos's `/v1/sessions/sovereign`:

* App passwords (`createAppPassword`/`listAppPasswords`/`revokeAppPassword`)
* Change handle (`updateHandle` + the wallet-signed alsoKnownAs op)
* Identity removal (`requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` + tombstone)
* **Blob restore** (`restore_blob_backup`'s `uploadBlob` leg — backup works everywhere, restore doesn't)

`SessionProvider::full_access_client`'s `NeedsUnlock` currently has exactly one resolution: the biometric passwordless `sovereignLogin`. Give it a second: on hosts without the `sovereignSessions` capability (<issue id="e2abaa52-2747-4daf-8c10-209294bd5183" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-454/phase-0b-custos-capability-extension-in-describeserver-self">MM-454</issue>), the unlock cue routes to a password `createSession` prompt (the machinery `source_login.rs` already uses transiently for claim/migration source login), persisting the resulting Bearer pair in the same versioned `{did}:oauth-tokens` record so refresh/rotation flows through the provider's existing ladder unchanged.

## Constraints

* ADR-0021 holds: identity ops need a full session; hosts may email-2FA (`AuthFactorTokenRequired` is already modeled in `PdsClient::create_session`).
* The password is used once and never stored — identical posture to the claim flow.
* Per-feature graceful degradation stays honest: a host that refuses an operation (e.g. no app-password support) surfaces the server's answer, not a wallet guess.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A claimed [bsky.social/reference-PDS](<http://bsky.social/reference-PDS>) identity can mint, list, and revoke app passwords; change handle; run account removal; and restore its blob backup — each behind the same biometric gates as the Custos paths.
2. `SessionError::NeedsUnlock` handling in the frontend branches on host capability: sovereign login (Custos) vs password prompt (other), with 2FA handled.

1	// pattern: Imperative Shell
2	//
3	// Gathers: a selected DID's persisted `oauth-tokens` record, current DID discovery,
4	//          and a per-DID coalescing lock
5	// Processes: restore a still-valid session, or rotate a near-expiry one via
6	//            `com.atproto.server.refreshSession` and atomically persist the new pair
7	// Returns: a ready full-access Bearer client, or a typed lifecycle error whose
8	//          `NEEDS_UNLOCK` variant hands off to the biometric sovereign login
9	
10	//! Per-DID full-access session lifecycle.
11	//!
12	//! [`SessionProvider::full_access_client`] is the seam every authenticated wallet
13	//! operation on a Custos-hosted identity goes through. It replaces the single
14	//! global in-memory `oauth_session` with an on-demand, per-DID resolver:
15	//!
16	//! 1. Load the selected DID's versioned [`SovereignTokenRecord`].
17	//! 2. If the access JWT is still valid, hand back a Bearer client directly — no
18	//!    network, so a restart (or an offline launch) with a live token needs no prompt.
19	//! 3. If it is expired/near-expiry but the refresh chain is alive, confirm the DID
20	//!    still resolves to the same host, then rotate exactly once via
21	//!    `refreshSession` and atomically persist the returned pair.
22	//! 4. If no usable refresh chain remains, return [`SessionError::NeedsUnlock`] — the
23	//!    frontend surfaces a passwordless "Unlock identity" action that runs the
24	//!    biometric-gated [`crate::sovereign_session::sovereign_login`].
25	//!
26	//! Concurrent callers for one DID coalesce behind a per-DID async lock: the first
27	//! rotates and persists, later callers re-read the freshly-stored record and reuse
28	//! it, so a refresh token can never be raced into replay detection.
29	
30	use std::collections::HashMap;
31	use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex, OnceLock};
32	
33	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
34	
35	use crate::identity_store::{IdentityStore, IdentityStoreError, SovereignTokenRecord};
36	use crate::oauth_client::OAuthClient;
37	use crate::pds_client::{PdsClient, PdsClientError};
38	use crate::sovereign_session::{audience_matches_server, bearer_jwt_claims};
39	
40	/// Seconds of headroom before an access token's `exp` at which it is treated as
41	/// already stale and proactively rotated. Covers clock skew plus the duration of
42	/// the operation the caller is about to perform, so a token cannot expire mid-flight.
43	const ACCESS_REFRESH_MARGIN_SECS: i64 = 120;
44	
45	/// Why a managed identity cannot produce a full-access client without a passwordless
46	/// unlock (a fresh device-key sovereign login).
47	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
48	#[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]
49	pub enum UnlockReason {
50	    /// No token record exists, the refresh token has itself expired, or the stored
51	    /// record is unusable (malformed or bound to another DID/host).
52	    NoRefreshChain,
53	    /// The hosting server rejected the refresh token (revoked/replayed). The dead
54	    /// record has been discarded.
55	    RefreshRevoked,
56	    /// The DID now resolves to a different PDS than the stored credentials' audience.
57	    /// The old-audience record has been discarded.
58	    HostChanged,
59	}
60	
61	/// Outcome of trying to obtain a full-access client for a managed DID.
62	///
63	/// Serializes as `{ "code": "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE", ... }` to match `OAuthError` /
64	/// `IdentityStoreError` / `SovereignLoginError`. Each variant is a distinct terminal
65	/// classification — the provider never loops refresh/login retries.
66	#[derive(Debug, Serialize, thiserror::Error)]
67	#[serde(
68	    tag = "code",
69	    rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE",
70	    rename_all_fields = "camelCase"
71	)]
72	pub enum SessionError {
73	    #[error("identity not found")]
74	    IdentityNotFound,
75	    #[error("identity is locked and needs a passwordless unlock")]
76	    NeedsUnlock { reason: UnlockReason },
77	    #[error("the hosting server rate limited the refresh")]
78	    RateLimited { retry_after: Option<String> },
79	    #[error("the identity's hosting server does not support session refresh")]
80	    UnsupportedHost,
81	    #[error("offline or transport failure: {message}")]
82	    Offline { message: String },
83	    #[error("hosting server failure: {status}")]
84	    ServerFailure { status: u16 },
85	    #[error("keychain failure: {message}")]
86	    Keychain { message: String },
87	    #[error("invalid session response: {message}")]
88	    InvalidResponse { message: String },
89	}
90	
91	/// A resolved, ready-to-use full-access session for one managed DID.
92	///
93	/// `client` is the authenticated XRPC vehicle for the downstream operation; the
94	/// summary fields let a thin Tauri command report status to the frontend without

140	/// Per-DID full-access session resolver.
141	///
142	/// Zero-sized, like [`IdentityStore`]: its only state is a process-global registry
143	/// of per-DID coalescing locks, so it is cheap to construct anywhere a resolve is
144	/// needed (Tauri commands, downstream operation modules, tests).
145	#[derive(Default)]
146	pub struct SessionProvider;

148	/// Return the coalescing lock for a DID, creating it on first use.
149	///
150	/// Different DIDs get independent locks (their sessions resolve concurrently); every
151	/// caller for one DID shares a single `tokio::Mutex`, held across the refresh await
152	/// so only one rotation is ever in flight. The registry map is guarded by a std
153	/// mutex held only long enough to clone the `Arc` — never across an await.
154	fn did_lock(did: &str) -> Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>> {
155	    static REGISTRY: OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>>> =
156	        OnceLock::new();
157	    let registry = REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
158	    let mut map = registry.lock().unwrap();
159	    map.entry(did.to_string())
160	        .or_insert_with(|| Arc::new(tokio::sync::Mutex::new(())))
161	        .clone()
162	}

164	fn map_store_error(error: IdentityStoreError) -> SessionError {
165	    match error {
166	        IdentityStoreError::IdentityNotFound => SessionError::IdentityNotFound,
167	        IdentityStoreError::KeychainError { message } => SessionError::Keychain { message },
168	        other => SessionError::Keychain {
169	            message: other.to_string(),
170	        },
171	    }
172	}

174	/// Map a DID-discovery failure to a session-lifecycle error. A transport failure
175	/// (offline, PDS unreachable) is [`SessionError::Offline`]; a resolution failure
176	/// (DID or PDS metadata absent) is [`SessionError::UnsupportedHost`]; a directory
177	/// throttle or HTTP verdict keeps its status-classified shape rather than reading
178	/// as a connectivity problem.
179	fn map_discovery_error(error: PdsClientError) -> SessionError {
180	    match error {
181	        PdsClientError::PdsUnreachable { reason } => SessionError::Offline { message: reason },
182	        PdsClientError::NetworkError { message } => SessionError::Offline { message },
183	        PdsClientError::DidNotFound | PdsClientError::InvalidResponse { .. } => {
184	            SessionError::UnsupportedHost
185	        }
186	        PdsClientError::RateLimited { retry_after, .. } => {
187	            SessionError::RateLimited { retry_after }
188	        }
189	        PdsClientError::XrpcError { status, .. } => SessionError::ServerFailure { status },
190	        PdsClientError::Unauthorized { .. } => SessionError::ServerFailure { status: 401 },
191	        other => SessionError::Offline {
192	            message: other.to_string(),
193	        },
194	    }
195	}

197	/// Whether two PDS URLs identify the same host (trailing slash is not significant).
198	fn pds_urls_match(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool {
199	    a.trim_end_matches('/') == b.trim_end_matches('/')
200	}

202	impl SessionProvider {
203	    /// Obtain a ready full-access client for `did`, refreshing or reporting a needed
204	    /// unlock as required. `now` is the current Unix time in seconds (injected so the
205	    /// expiry ladder is deterministic in tests).
206	    ///
207	    /// The entire decision runs under the DID's coalescing lock, and the token record
208	    /// is re-read *inside* the lock so a caller that waited on an in-flight rotation
209	    /// observes the freshly-persisted pair instead of racing a second refresh.
210	    pub async fn full_access_client(
211	        &self,
212	        pds_client: &PdsClient,
213	        store: &IdentityStore,
214	        did: &str,
215	        now: i64,
216	    ) -> Result<ActiveSession, SessionError> {
217	        let lock = did_lock(did);
218	        let _guard = lock.lock().await;
219	
220	        let Some(record) = store.load_oauth_tokens(did).map_err(map_store_error)? else {
221	            return Err(SessionError::NeedsUnlock {
222	                reason: UnlockReason::NoRefreshChain,
223	            });
224	        };
225	
226	        // The stored access JWT must be readable and bound to this DID + host, or the
227	        // record is corrupt/foreign and only a fresh mint can recover it.
228	        let Some(access) = bearer_jwt_claims(&record.access_jwt) else {
229	            store.delete_oauth_tokens(did).map_err(map_store_error)?;
230	            return Err(SessionError::NeedsUnlock {
231	                reason: UnlockReason::NoRefreshChain,
232	            });
233	        };
234	        if access.sub != did
235	            || !audience_matches_server(&access.aud, &record.server_did, &record.pds_url)
236	        {
237	            store.delete_oauth_tokens(did).map_err(map_store_error)?;
238	            return Err(SessionError::NeedsUnlock {
239	                reason: UnlockReason::NoRefreshChain,
240	            });
241	        }
242	
243	        // Fast path: a still-valid access token is usable directly — no discovery, no
244	        // network — which is what lets a restart (or an offline launch) skip the prompt.
245	        if (access.exp as i64) > now + ACCESS_REFRESH_MARGIN_SECS {
246	            return active_session_from_record(did, record, false);
247	        }
248	
249	        // Rotation is needed. Without a live refresh token there is no chain to rotate.
250	        let refresh_exp = record
251	            .refresh_expires_at
252	            .or_else(|| bearer_jwt_claims(&record.refresh_jwt).map(|c| c.exp));
253	        if refresh_exp.is_none_or(|exp| (exp as i64) <= now) {
254	            return Err(SessionError::NeedsUnlock {
255	                reason: UnlockReason::NoRefreshChain,
256	            });
257	        }
258	
259	        // Validate the DID still resolves to this record's host before sending the
260	        // refresh token — a migrated/changed host means the stored credential is for a
261	        // stale audience and must be discarded rather than presented.
262	        let (current_pds, _doc) = pds_client
263	            .discover_pds(did)
264	            .await
265	            .map_err(map_discovery_error)?;
266	        if !pds_urls_match(&current_pds, &record.pds_url) {
267	            store.delete_oauth_tokens(did).map_err(map_store_error)?;
268	            return Err(SessionError::NeedsUnlock {
269	                reason: UnlockReason::HostChanged,
270	            });
271	        }
272	
273	        rotate_and_persist(pds_client, store, did, &record, now).await
274	    }
275	}

277	/// Tauri command: pre-flight a managed identity's full-access session for the UI.
278	///
279	/// Restores or rotates the selected DID's session and reports its status, discarding
280	/// the resolved client (an [`OAuthClient`] cannot cross the IPC boundary). The
281	/// frontend calls this when showing an identity so a `NEEDS_UNLOCK` result can render
282	/// the passwordless "Unlock identity" action before the user attempts an operation.
283	#[tauri::command]
284	pub async fn ensure_identity_session(
285	    state: tauri::State<'_, crate::oauth::AppState>,
286	    did: String,
287	) -> Result<SessionReady, SessionError> {
288	    let now =
289	        crate::sovereign_session::unix_timestamp().map_err(|_| SessionError::InvalidResponse {
290	            message: "system clock is unavailable".into(),
291	        })?;
292	    let session = SessionProvider
293	        .full_access_client(state.pds_client(), &IdentityStore, &did, now)
294	        .await?;
295	    Ok(SessionReady::from(&session))

298	/// Rebuild a Bearer [`OAuthClient`] plus its status summary from a token record.
299	/// Shared by the still-valid fast path and the post-rotation path.
300	fn active_session_from_record(
301	    did: &str,
302	    record: SovereignTokenRecord,
303	    rotated: bool,
304	) -> Result<ActiveSession, SessionError> {
305	    let access =
306	        bearer_jwt_claims(&record.access_jwt).ok_or_else(|| SessionError::InvalidResponse {
307	            message: "stored accessJwt is malformed".into(),
308	        })?;
309	    let client = OAuthClient::new_bearer(
310	        record.access_jwt.clone(),
311	        record.refresh_jwt.clone(),
312	        record.pds_url.clone(),
313	    )

315	        message: e.to_string(),
316	    })?;
317	    Ok(ActiveSession {
318	        client,
319	        did: did.to_string(),
320	        pds_url: record.pds_url,
321	        access_expires_at: access.exp,
322	        refresh_expires_at: record.refresh_expires_at,
323	        rotated,
324	    })
325	}

327	/// Rotate a near-expiry pair via `com.atproto.server.refreshSession` and atomically
328	/// persist the returned pair. Exactly one network attempt — no retry loop.
329	async fn rotate_and_persist(
330	    pds_client: &PdsClient,
331	    store: &IdentityStore,
332	    did: &str,
333	    record: &SovereignTokenRecord,
334	    now: i64,
335	) -> Result<ActiveSession, SessionError> {
336	    let url = format!(
337	        "{}/xrpc/com.atproto.server.refreshSession",
338	        record.pds_url.trim_end_matches('/')
339	    );
340	    let response = pds_client
341	        .client()
342	        .post(url.as_str())
343	        .header(
344	            reqwest::header::AUTHORIZATION,
345	            format!("Bearer {}", record.refresh_jwt),
346	        )
347	        .send()
348	        .await
349	        .map_err(|e| {
350	            // Strip the URL from the error before it becomes a message: a reqwest error's
351	            // `Display` embeds the full request URL, which can carry account material.
352	            let e = e.without_url();
353	            // Redacted breadcrumb so a refresh transport failure is visible in diagnostics —
354	            // it otherwise records nothing and surfaces only as a generic offline error.
355	            crate::diagnostics::record_transport(
356	                "refreshSession",
357	                reqwest::Url::parse(&url)
358	                    .ok()
359	                    .and_then(|u| u.host_str().map(str::to_string))
360	                    .as_deref(),
361	                crate::diagnostics::transport_category(&e),
362	            );
363	            SessionError::Offline {
364	                message: e.to_string(),
365	            }
366	        })?;
367	
368	    let status = response.status();
369	    if !status.is_success() {
370	        let retry_after = response
371	            .headers()
372	            .get(reqwest::header::RETRY_AFTER)
373	            .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok())
374	            .map(str::to_string);
375	        return Err(classify_refresh_failure(
376	            status.as_u16(),
377	            retry_after,
378	            store,
379	            did,
380	        )?);
381	    }
382	
383	    let refreshed: RefreshSessionResponse =
384	        response
385	            .json()
386	            .await
387	            .map_err(|e| SessionError::InvalidResponse {
388	                message: e.to_string(),
389	            })?;
390	
391	    // Bind the rotated pair to the same DID and hosting server the record was minted
392	    // for — a rotation must never silently re-audience the session.
393	    if refreshed.did != did {
394	        return Err(SessionError::InvalidResponse {
395	            message: "refreshSession returned a different DID".into(),
396	        });
397	    }
398	    let access =
399	        bearer_jwt_claims(&refreshed.access_jwt).ok_or_else(|| SessionError::InvalidResponse {
400	            message: "rotated accessJwt is missing valid claims".into(),
401	        })?;
402	    let refresh =
403	        bearer_jwt_claims(&refreshed.refresh_jwt).ok_or_else(|| SessionError::InvalidResponse {
404	            message: "rotated refreshJwt is missing valid claims".into(),
405	        })?;
406	    if access.sub != did || refresh.sub != did {
407	        return Err(SessionError::InvalidResponse {
408	            message: "rotated tokens are bound to a different DID".into(),
409	        });
410	    }
411	    if !audience_matches_server(&access.aud, &record.server_did, &record.pds_url)
412	        || !audience_matches_server(&refresh.aud, &record.server_did, &record.pds_url)
413	    {
414	        return Err(SessionError::InvalidResponse {
415	            message: "rotated tokens are bound to a different host".into(),
416	        });
417	    }
418	
419	    let stored_at = u64::try_from(now).map_err(|_| SessionError::InvalidResponse {
420	        message: "negative timestamp cannot be persisted".into(),
421	    })?;
422	    let new_record = SovereignTokenRecord {
423	        version: SovereignTokenRecord::VERSION,
424	        access_jwt: refreshed.access_jwt,
425	        refresh_jwt: refreshed.refresh_jwt,
426	        pds_url: record.pds_url.clone(),
427	        server_did: record.server_did.clone(),
428	        access_expires_at: Some(access.exp),
429	        refresh_expires_at: Some(refresh.exp),
430	        stored_at,
431	    };
432	    store
433	        .store_oauth_tokens(did, &new_record)
434	        .map_err(map_store_error)?;
435	
436	    active_session_from_record(did, new_record, true)
437	}

439	/// Classify a non-success `refreshSession` response into a distinct terminal error.
440	///
441	/// A rejected refresh token (400/401) is revoked/replayed — the dead record is
442	/// discarded and the identity falls back to a passwordless unlock. Rate limiting,
443	/// an unsupported host, and other server failures each stay recognizable so the UI
444	/// (and downstream callers) never collapse them into one another. Returns `Err` only
445	/// if discarding the dead record itself fails.
446	fn classify_refresh_failure(
447	    status: u16,
448	    retry_after: Option<String>,
449	    store: &IdentityStore,
450	    did: &str,
451	) -> Result<SessionError, SessionError> {
452	    Ok(match status {
453	        400 | 401 => {
454	            store.delete_oauth_tokens(did).map_err(map_store_error)?;
455	            SessionError::NeedsUnlock {
456	                reason: UnlockReason::RefreshRevoked,
457	            }
458	        }
459	        404 | 405 => SessionError::UnsupportedHost,
460	        429 => SessionError::RateLimited { retry_after },
461	        other => SessionError::ServerFailure { status: other },
462	    })
463	}

# Obsign (identity-wallet) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-08
Last updated: 2026-07-20

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS application — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend running in a native WKWebView, communicating with a Rust backend exclusively through Tauri's IPC bridge.

## Browser test harness (drive the app without a simulator)

The whole frontend runs in a plain desktop browser under `vite dev` — the only thing the
browser lacks is the Tauri `invoke()` seam, which the harness intercepts with Tauri's
official `mockIPC`. This lets an agent (or a human) reach every screen and reproduce any
state, including rare error states, without a Mac/Xcode/simulator. Design + acceptance
criteria: [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md).

**Start it** (or use the `.claude/launch.json` config `wallet-harness` / `wallet-harness-proxy`):
- **Fake mode** (default, no backend needed): `pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness` → http://localhost:5173.
- **Proxy mode** (real thin-HTTP calls against a hermetic local PDS): in one terminal
  `cargo build -p pds` then `just harness-pds` (prints the URL + admin token); in another,
  `VITE_HARNESS_PDS_URL=<url> VITE_HARNESS_ADMIN_TOKEN=<token> pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness:proxy`.
- Plain `pnpm dev` never activates the harness (double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS`);
  `pnpm check:harness-absence` proves it is tree-shaken out of production builds.

**`window.__harness` console API** (both modes):
- `.scenario(name)` — switch preset and reload (persists across reload). Presets:
  `fresh-install`, `foreign-pds` (a spec-compliant non-Custos host — advertises no
  capabilities, so the create flow's gate closes and steers to import),
  `unreachable-pds` (the same empty capability list, but `reached: false` — the gate must
  show a retryable error, never the steer), `one-identity`, `multi-identity`,
  `alert-active`, `device-key-unusable` (a device restored from an encrypted backup: the
  device-key metadata came back, the Secure Enclave key did not — the only way to reach the
  "can no longer sign" degraded state in a browser with no enclave), `migration-in-flight`,
  `agent-connected`, `app-password-minted`, plus the share-recovery matrix:
  `recover-escrow` (happy path A — iCloud Share 1 + zero-delay escrow release),
  `recover-sovereign` (happy path B — manual Share 3 entry; paste
  `state().recovery.fixtures.share3Words` or `.share3`), `recover-wrong-set`
  (`fixtures.wrongSet` → SHARE_SET_MISMATCH), `recover-corrupt-share`
  (`fixtures.corrupt` → SHARE_CHECKSUM), `recover-mismatch` (verification fails —
  shares don't match the identity), `recover-pending-delay` (24h escrow window; the
  second poll releases), `recover-cancelled` (pending release cancelled → uniform
  401 on poll), `recover-epilogue-resume` (launch resumes an interrupted rotation
  epilogue); plus the escrow-less kit pair: `self-held-kit` (a claimed identity on a
  non-Custos host — device key at `rotationKeys[0]`, a longer claimed tail than the
  re-key's `[device, PDS]`, no recovery key, host advertises nothing) and
  `self-held-kit-escrow-host` (the same identity after the kit, now hosted somewhere that
  DOES advertise `escrow` — the upsell seam's only true state). `.scenarios` lists them.
- `.failNext(command, error)` — make the next call of `command` reject with a typed error,
  e.g. `window.__harness.failNext('create_account', { code: 'EXPIRED_CODE' })`.
- `.emit(event, payload)` — deliver a Tauri event to live `listen()` subscribers;
  `window.__harness.emit('auth_ready')` simulates the OAuth deep-link return.
- `.state()` — a read-only snapshot of the fake store. `.mode` is `'fake'` or `'proxy'`.

**Proxy mode is real only for the thin-HTTP subset** — `create_account` (mints + redeems a
real claim code, POSTs `/v1/accounts/mobile`) and `get_available_user_domains`
(describeServer). By the honest boundary, these stay **faked even in proxy mode** (heavy
Rust logic with no thin-HTTP form): the DID ceremony (`perform_did_ceremony`,
`*_did_web_ceremony`), OAuth completion (`prepare/complete_oauth_flow`), the migration
transfer legs (`transfer_repo`/`transfer_blobs`/…, `finalize_migration`), recovery/claim
PLC ops, and the agent surfaces (which need a real post-ceremony session the faked
ceremony never mints). Fidelity the browser can never cover: real Keychain/Secure-Enclave,
the biometric prompt, ASWebAuthenticationSession, WKWebView rendering, safe-area insets,
camera/QR — those stay simulator/device concerns.

**Fake handler coverage is enforced:** every command in `$lib/ipc` must have a handler in
`src/lib/harness/registry.ts` or `registry.test.ts` fails (`pnpm test`). Harness code lives
in `src/lib/harness/` (`install`/`registry`/`state`/`scenarios`/`control` + `proxy/`),
activated by `src/hooks.client.ts`.

- `pnpm install` has been run in `apps/identity-wallet/`
- Node.js 22.x is in PATH (provided by the Nix dev shell)

### Rust Backend (src-tauri/)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib.rs::create_account(claim_code, email, handle) -> Result<CreateAccountResult, CreateAccountError>` — Tauri IPC command: gets or creates device key via `device_key::get_or_create()`, POSTs to PDS `/v1/accounts/mobile`, stores tokens in Keychain on success
- `src/lib.rs::perform_did_ceremony(handle: String, password: String) -> Result<DIDCeremonyResult, DIDCeremonyError>` — Tauri IPC command running the **client-share ceremony** (ceremony inversion): fetches the PDS signing key (GET /v1/repo-signing-key), loads-or-generates the client-side share set via `share_ceremony::load_or_create` (recovery seed + `derive_recovery_keypair` + 2-of-3 v2 envelope split, staged in the `ceremony-staging` Keychain slot BEFORE any network call so a retry reuses the identical set/set_id), builds the signed did:plc genesis op via `crypto::build_did_plc_genesis_op_multi_rotation_with_external_signer` with `rotationKeys = [device, recovery, PDS]` (ADR-0027) using the device key as signer, POSTs the op + password + `recoveryKey` + `escrowShare` (the Share 2 envelope — the only share Custos ever sees) to POST /v1/dids, persists DID + upgraded session token in Keychain, writes the wallet-generated Share 1 envelope to the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with a read-back verify (same convention as the re-key flow, so a second identity's ceremony cannot overwrite the first's Share 1), and returns `{ did, share3, share3Words }` to the frontend
- `src/lib.rs::confirm_share_backup(did: String) -> Result<(), ShareBackupError>` — Tauri IPC command: the ceremony teardown gate. Verifies the ceremony DID's Share 1 is durably present in `recovery-share-1:{did}` (else `SHARE_NOT_STORED` — the staging slot must not be destroyed while it is the seed's only home), then deletes the `ceremony-staging` slot (the seed's and Share 2's last local copy). The `did` is threaded from the ceremony result so the check reads the exact identity just created (mirrors the re-key epilogue's `confirm_rekey`). Idempotent; invoked by the frontend when the Shamir backup screen's confirmation completes
- `src/share_ceremony.rs` — client-side share generation module: `CeremonyShareSet` (recovery key did:key + the three base32 envelope strings + the Share 3 word phrase, all share material in `Zeroizing`), `load_or_create(handle, pds_url)` (reuse a valid staged set or generate + stage a fresh one; the staging record stores the three envelopes only — the seed is recomputed via `combine_envelopes(share1, share2)` on load), `clear_staging()` (idempotent teardown), `STAGING_ACCOUNT` (`"ceremony-staging"`). **Fail-closed staging contract:** only a genuinely absent slot, or one staged for different ceremony inputs (a new handle/PDS is the user's explicit abandonment of the old attempt), permits fresh generation; a present-but-unreadable/corrupt record errors with `StagingCorrupt` and preserves the slot — it may be the exact set a prior attempt already bound to a genesis op and escrowed, so overwriting it would permanently destroy the recovery seed
- `src/share_recovery.rs` — the "Recover existing identity" ceremony (10 Tauri IPC commands), the consuming inverse of `share_ceremony.rs`: `start_share_recovery(identifier)` (resolve handle/did:plc via plc.directory, then auto-load Share 1 via `auto_load_share1`: the resolved DID's iCloud-synchronizable per-DID slot, then its device-local per-DID slot, then the legacy global `recovery-share-1`, taking the first tier holding a valid v2 index-1 envelope), `add_recovery_share(share)` (base32 or word-phrase entry; SHARE_CHECKSUM, SHARE_SET_MISMATCH — with both set_ids — and DUPLICATE_SHARE are distinct, pre-combine errors), `remove_recovery_share(index)`, the escrow-assisted path client `initiate_escrow_release()` / `request_escrow_release(otp?)` (targets the account's own PDS endpoint from the authoritative DID state; OTP opens the release, OTP-less calls poll the pending window; the server's uniform 401 maps to RELEASE_UNAUTHORIZED), `verify_recovery_shares()` (combine → `derive_recovery_keypair` → compare against the **authoritative plc.directory audit log**, never a cached doc — mismatch is SHARES_DO_NOT_MATCH_IDENTITY, before anything signs), `recover_identity()` (fresh per-DID device key; the recovery key signs the rotation op installing it at `rotationKeys[0]`; talks ONLY to plc.directory — the fully-sovereign path makes zero PDS requests until re-escrow; idempotent on retry; durably stages the epilogue before returning), `run_recovery_epilogue(skip_escrow?)` (resumable: swap the new recovery key into `rotationKeys[1]` signed by the new device key → re-escrow the new Share 2 over a stored-or-fresh device-key sovereign session → rewrite the recovered DID's per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` with read-back verify; each step recorded in the durable `recovery-epilogue` Keychain record as it completes), `get_pending_recovery_epilogue()` (launch-time resume hook), `confirm_recovery_backup()` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_share_backup`; destroys the epilogue record only after the NEW Share 1 is verified durable in the per-DID slot). Session state (`AppState.share_recovery_state`) is in-memory by design — the pre-anchor phase restarts from the entry screen; only the epilogue persists. `ShareRecoveryError` serializes as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/lib.rs::{prepare_did_web_ceremony,complete_did_web_ceremony}` — did:web sibling ceremony: obtains the same device key and pending account's reserved repo key, lets the frontend compose/export the reviewed `did.json`, then submits it to `POST /v1/dids` only after it is externally resolvable. Completion persists the upgraded session and the server-returned Shamir Share 1 into the per-DID slot `recovery-share-1:{did}` (the same convention as the client-share and re-key paths); managed-hosting selection then opts the account into `/v1/did-web/hosting`.
- `src/lib.rs::import_did_web_identity(input) -> Result<ImportedDidWebIdentity, ImportDidWebError>` — bring an EXISTING did:web under wallet management so the method-agnostic flows (outbound migration first) can operate on it. There is no claim ceremony for did:web: control is proven by the domain publish and the later source-PDS password, so "import" is `normalize_did_web_input` (accepts `example.com` / `https://…` / `did:web:…`, mirroring the frontend's `didWebFromDomain`) → `PdsClient::discover_pds` to resolve + validate the live document → `persist_imported_did_web` (registers the DID, mints its per-DID device key so `detect_migration_path` classifies it `SelfSigned`, and caches a PLC-shaped doc with an **empty `rotationKeys`** — a did:web has none, and showing the device key as a root key before the migration leg publishes it as `#device` would be a lie). Idempotent — re-importing refreshes the cached doc. `ImportDidWebError` (INVALID_DOMAIN, DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_DOCUMENT, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR, KEYCHAIN_ERROR). The did:web outbound-migration identity leg itself lives in `migrate.rs::{build_did_web_migration_document_cmd,submit_did_web_migration_document_cmd}` (the wallet composes the reviewed `did.json`, and submission verifies it is externally resolvable before adopting the identity)
- `src/oauth.rs` — OAuth PKCE client module: `AppState` (pending_login + oauth_session mutexes + custos_client OnceLock + pds_client + claim_state + recovery_state + migration_state + orchestration_state; both source logins — the claim flow and the outbound migration — are password-based `createSession`, so neither parks OAuth state — see `claim::authenticate_source_pds` / `migration_orchestrator::authenticate_migration_source`), `OAuthSession` (access/refresh/expiry/nonce), `DPoPKeypair` (P-256, persisted in Keychain), `OAuthError` enum, PKCE utilities (verifier + S256 challenge), `OAuthPrepared` (the `{authUrl, callbackScheme}` returned to the frontend), `prepare_oauth_flow` + `complete_oauth_flow` (the create-flow login split around the in-app auth session: prepare does DPoP keygen/PKCE/PAR → authorize URL and parks the verifier+CSRF in `pending_login`; complete validates the callback URL + does the token exchange), `parse_callback_url` (shared callback-URL parser, `pub(crate)`); `AppState::pds_client()` accessor exposes `PdsClient` for claim flow commands
- `src/claim.rs` — PLC rotation key claim flow module (5 Tauri IPC commands): `resolve_identity(handle_or_did) -> Result<IdentityInfo, ResolveError>` (resolves handle/DID to identity info via plc.directory, stores ClaimState), `authenticate_source_pds(did, identifier, password, auth_factor_token?) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (**password `createSession`** against the source PDS → full-session Bearer `OAuthClient` stored in ClaimState; the next steps are PLC/identity ops that no OAuth `transition:generic` token can drive, so a full session is required — ADR-0021; the password is used once and never stored. An email-2FA account returns `TwoFactorRequired` on the token-less attempt — the PDS emails a code and the UI re-invokes with `auth_factor_token`), `request_claim_verification(did) -> Result<(), ClaimError>` (calls `requestPlcOperationSignature` XRPC on old PDS to trigger email verification), `sign_and_verify_claim(did, token) -> Result<VerifiedClaimOp, ClaimError>` (calls `getRecommendedDidCredentials` and `signPlcOperation` on old PDS, fetches audit log, verifies signature + 4-point local checks, stores signed op in ClaimState), `submit_claim(did) -> Result<ClaimResult, ClaimError>` (POSTs signed op to plc.directory, persists identity to IdentityStore, clears ClaimState). Types: `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ClaimState`. Error enums: `ResolveError` (HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR), `ClaimError` (INVALID_TOKEN, VERIFICATION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, UNAUTHORIZED, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/oauth_client.rs` — `OAuthClient`: authenticated HTTP client supporting two auth modes selected at construction (private `AuthMode` enum): `new(session, base_url)` builds a **DPoP** client (wraps every request with `Authorization: DPoP {access_token}` + a `DPoP` proof header, transparent lazy refresh when the token has <60s remaining, automatic retry on `use_dpop_nonce` 400 responses); `new_bearer(access_jwt, refresh_jwt, base_url)` builds a **Bearer** client (`Authorization: Bearer {access_jwt}`, no DPoP proof/nonce dance, expiry derived from the access JWT's `exp` claim) — used for the migration destination-PDS session, which is created via a service-auth `createAccount` rather than an OAuth flow. Methods: `get(path)`, `post(path, body)` (JSON), `post_no_body(path)` (zero bytes, no `Content-Type` — for no-input XRPC procedures like `requestPlcOperationSignature`/`activateAccount`, whose lexicons define no input; a spec-strict PDS rejects any body), `post_bytes(path, content_type, body)` (raw byte body — CAR repo import + blob upload)
- `src/device_key.rs` — P-256 device key management with `#[cfg]`-based dispatch: macOS/simulator uses software keys via `crypto` crate + Keychain storage; real iOS device uses Secure Enclave via `security-framework`. Public API: `get_or_create() -> Result<DevicePublicKey, DeviceKeyError>` (idempotent), `sign(data) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DeviceKeyError>`. Exposes `pub(crate)` account-name consts `DEVICE_KEY_PRIV_ACCOUNT` / `DEVICE_KEY_PUB_ACCOUNT` / `DEVICE_KEY_APP_LABEL_ACCOUNT` (single source of truth for the global device-key Keychain accounts; copied into per-DID slots by `IdentityStore::adopt_global_device_key`)
- `src/keychain.rs` — iOS Keychain abstraction (`store_item`, `get_item`, `delete_item`) under service `"ezpds-identity-wallet"`; PDS URL helpers: `store_pds_url`/`load_pds_url` (PDS base URL); OAuth helpers: `store_dpop_key`/`load_dpop_key` (P-256 DPoP private key scalar), `store_oauth_tokens`/`load_oauth_tokens` (access + refresh token pair)
- `src/http.rs` — `CustosClient` with runtime-configurable base URL (initialized via `AppState::set_custos_client(url)` on first launch; localhost:8080 debug fallback); methods: `post()`, `get()`, `post_with_bearer()`, `par()` (POST /oauth/par with DPoP proof), `token_exchange()` (POST /oauth/token with PKCE verifier); response types: `ParResponse`, `TokenResponse`, `TokenErrorResponse`
- `src/identity_store.rs` — `IdentityStore` unit struct for multi-identity Keychain management with per-DID namespacing. Public API: `add_identity(did)` (registers DID in managed-dids index), `remove_identity(did)` (deletes DID and all per-DID entries), `list_identities()` (returns managed DIDs), `get_or_create_device_key(did)` (lazy per-DID P-256 key generation), `adopt_global_device_key(did)` (aliases the per-DID device key to the global `device_key.rs` key by copying its Keychain material into the per-DID slot — used by the create flow, whose genesis op is signed with the global key before the DID exists), `store_did_doc(did, json)` / `get_did_doc(did)` (DID document persistence), `store_plc_log(did, json)` / `get_plc_log(did)` (PLC audit log persistence), and `store_oauth_tokens(did, record)` / `load_oauth_tokens(did)` / `delete_oauth_tokens(did)` for the versioned full-access Bearer session in `{did}:oauth-tokens`. All methods require DID to be registered first (returns `IdentityNotFound` otherwise). `IdentityStoreError` enum: IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, IDENTITY_ALREADY_EXISTS, KEYCHAIN_ERROR, KEY_GENERATION_FAILED, SERIALIZATION_ERROR, DEVICE_KEY_UNUSABLE (serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`)
- `src/sovereign_session.rs` — per-DID Custos sovereign login: discovers the selected DID's current PDS and server DID, signs the shared canonical envelope with that DID's device key, validates the response DID and JWT subject/audience, persists a versioned `SovereignTokenRecord`, and exposes `stored_bearer_client(did)` for authenticated XRPC helpers. `sovereign_login` is the narrow Tauri command; the typed frontend `sovereignLogin(did)` wrapper performs the biometric gate before invoking it. The `pub(crate)` JWT/audience helpers (`bearer_jwt_claims`, `audience_matches_server`) are the single source of the sub/aud binding check, reused by `session_provider`.
- `src/session_provider.rs` — per-DID full-access **session lifecycle** (the seam every authenticated Custos-hosted operation goes through; the minimum contract). `SessionProvider::full_access_client(pds_client, store, did, now) -> Result<ActiveSession, SessionError>` runs a decision ladder under a per-DID coalescing lock: (1) no record / dead refresh → `NeedsUnlock{NoRefreshChain}`; (2) access JWT still valid (`exp > now + 120s`) → rebuild a Bearer client **with no network** (this is what makes a restart or offline launch with a live token need no prompt); (3) near-expiry with a live refresh → discover the DID's current PDS, and if the host moved **discard the old-audience record** + `NeedsUnlock{HostChanged}`, else call `com.atproto.server.refreshSession` exactly once and atomically persist the rotated pair (re-validating sub/aud). Distinct terminal errors, never looped: `NeedsUnlock{reason}`, `RateLimited{retryAfter}`, `UnsupportedHost`, `Offline{message}`, `ServerFailure{status}`, `Keychain`, `InvalidResponse`. A revoked refresh (400/401) and a host change both delete the dead record; a rate limit keeps it. Coalescing is a re-read (not a shared future): the second caller for one DID waits on the lock, then re-loads the freshly-persisted record — so a refresh token can never be raced into replay detection. Does NOT reuse `OAuthClient::refresh_token_bearer` (which is in-memory-only by design) — the provider owns refresh+persist. Types: `ActiveSession` { client, did, pds_url, access_expires_at, refresh_expires_at, rotated }, `SessionReady` (serializable summary, drops the client), `UnlockReason` (NO_REFRESH_CHAIN / REFRESH_REVOKED / HOST_CHANGED), `SessionError` (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE `code`). The coalescing lock registry is a process-global `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<did, Arc<tokio::Mutex>>>>` (unit-struct-over-global shape, like `IdentityStore`).
- `src/pds_client.rs` — PDS discovery and OAuth module for arbitrary PDS endpoints (not just our PDS). `PdsClient` struct (stateless, wraps a `reqwest::Client` + plc.directory URL). Public API: `plc_directory_url() -> &str` (returns the plc.directory base URL), `client() -> &Client` (returns the inner reqwest client), `resolve_handle(handle) -> Result<String, PdsClientError>` (DNS TXT `_atproto.{handle}` with HTTP `/.well-known/atproto-did` fallback), `discover_pds(did) -> Result<(String, PlcDidDocument), PdsClientError>` (fetches DID doc from plc.directory, extracts `atproto_pds` endpoint, verifies reachability via HEAD), `discover_auth_server(pds_url) -> Result<AuthServerMetadata, PdsClientError>` (fetches `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, validates `code` response type + S256 challenge method), `pds_par(metadata, pkce_challenge, state, dpop_proof, dpop_jkt, login_hint?) -> Result<PdsParResponse, PdsClientError>` (PAR to arbitrary PDS), `pds_token_exchange(metadata, code, pkce_verifier, dpop_proof) -> Result<reqwest::Response, PdsClientError>` (returns raw response for caller nonce-retry), `build_pds_authorize_url(metadata, request_uri, login_hint?) -> String` (constructs browser redirect URL), `fetch_audit_log(did) -> Result<String, PdsClientError>` (fetches PLC operation audit log as raw JSON from `{plc_directory_url}/{did}/log/audit`), `post_plc_operation(did, operation) -> Result<(), PdsClientError>` (POSTs signed PLC operation JSON to `{plc_directory_url}/{did}`), `describe_server(pds_url) -> Result<DescribeServerResponse, PdsClientError>` (GET `com.atproto.server.describeServer` — probes an arbitrary PDS for its `did`/available-user-domains before migration, and records the response's optional `custos` capability extension into `pds_capabilities`'s per-host cache), `create_session(pds_url, identifier, password, auth_factor_token?) -> Result<CreateSessionResponse, PdsClientError>` (POST `com.atproto.server.createSession` — the claim flow's password source login; a 401 maps to `PdsClientError::InvalidCredentials`, or `AuthFactorTokenRequired` when the account has email 2FA and no code was supplied; the returned JWTs feed `OAuthClient::new_bearer`). Module-level XRPC functions (take `&OAuthClient`): the claim helpers `request_plc_operation_signature(client)`, `sign_plc_operation(client, request)`, `get_recommended_did_credentials(client)`; and the outbound-migration helpers `get_service_auth(client, aud, lxm)`, `create_account_migration(client, request)` (maps HTTP 409 → `PdsClientError::DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `import_repo(client, car_bytes)`, `upload_blob(client, mime, bytes)`, `list_missing_blobs(client, cursor)`, `get_preferences(client)`, `put_preferences(client, prefs)`, `check_account_status(client)`, `activate_account(client)`, `deactivate_account(client)`. Every authenticated XRPC helper routes its non-2xx branch through the private `classify_xrpc_response(context, resp)` (→ pure `classify_xrpc_error(status, retry_after, body)`), so a server response is classified by status — `429 → RateLimited{retry_after}`, `401 → Unauthorized`, else `XrpcError{status, error, message}` carrying the atproto error envelope — instead of being flattened into `NetworkError`. `NetworkError` is now transport-only. Types: `PlcDidDocument` (Clone), `PlcService` (Clone), `AuthServerMetadata`, `PdsParResponse`, `SignPlcOperationRequest`, `SignPlcOperationResponse`, `RecommendedCredentials`, plus migration types `DescribeServerResponse`, `ServiceAuthToken`, `CreateAccountMigrationRequest`, `CreateAccountResponse`, `CreateSessionResponse`, `MissingBlob`/`MissingBlobs`, `UploadBlobResponse`, `AccountStatus` (from `checkAccountStatus`). `PdsClientError` enum: HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, UNAUTHORIZED, XRPC_ERROR, INVALID_RESPONSE, OAUTH_FAILED, DID_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, AUTH_FACTOR_TOKEN_REQUIRED, INSECURE_PDS_URL (serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`)
- `src/plc_monitor.rs` — PLC monitoring module: `PlcMonitor` (borrows `PdsClient`; `check_all()` iterates all managed DIDs, `check_for_changes(did)` diffs current audit log against cached log and classifies new entries as authorized/unauthorized by verifying signatures against the device key); `run_monitoring_loop(app_handle)` (spawned once at app startup, checks every 15 minutes via `tokio::time::interval` with `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`, emits `"plc_alert"` Tauri event to frontend when unauthorized changes detected); `check_identity_status` (Tauri IPC command: synchronous foreground check of all managed identities, returns `Vec<IdentityStatus>`). Types: `UnauthorizedChange` { cid, created_at, signing_key, operation } (camelCase serialization), `IdentityStatus` { did, alert_count, unauthorized_changes } (camelCase serialization), `MonitorError` { NetworkError, IdentityStoreError, ParseError } (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE tag serialization)
- `src/agents.rs` — Agent consent + audit module (5 **per-identity** Tauri IPC commands, the wallet side of the auth.md claim ceremony + "My agents"): `preview_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimPreview` (POST `/v1/agents/claim-preview` — what approving would grant, shown before the biometric gate), `confirm_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimConfirmation` (POST `/agent/identity/claim/confirm` — the human gate; the frontend wraps it in `authenticateBiometric()`), `list_agents(did) -> Vec<AgentSummary>`, `revoke_agent(did, registration_id)`, `get_agent_audit(did, registration_id, cursor?) -> AgentAuditPage`. Each takes a `did` and resolves a **refreshable per-DID full-access session** via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (like `app_passwords.rs`) — issuing the request through `session.client` (`OAuthClient`), so an expired session self-heals via `refreshSession` or, failing that, `SESSION_LOCKED{reason}` cues the frontend to run the biometric `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry. This replaces the previous auth on the never-refreshed global `"session-token"`, whose lapse dead-ended every agent command as a bogus connection error. Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&OAuthClient`, tested against httpmock. `AgentsError` (NOT_AUTHENTICATED, CODE_NOT_FOUND, CODE_EXPIRED, ALREADY_CLAIMED, ACCESS_DENIED, AGENT_NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED, SESSION_LOCKED, NETWORK_ERROR, UNKNOWN) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`; the ceremony's `{error}` codes map onto it in `map_ceremony_error`, and a session-lifecycle failure via `map_session_error` (only a genuine transport failure is NETWORK_ERROR — a NeedsUnlock is SESSION_LOCKED, every other verdict is UNKNOWN), so denial/expiry/lock render as explicit states
- `src/oauth_consent.rs` — Wallet-confirmed OAuth consent client (3 **per-identity** Tauri IPC commands, the wallet side of the pending-authorization primitive — Phases A + B of the wallet-confirmed-OAuth-consent design plan): `preview_oauth_consent(did, user_code) -> ConsentPreview` (resolves the selected DID's hosting PDS via `discover_pds`, `GET /oauth/authorize/consent-request?user_code=…` — what approving would grant: client name/id, redirect URI, requesting origin/IP, requested scope list, `login_hint` — shown before the biometric gate), `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id(did, request_id) -> ConsentPreview` (Phase B QR-scan path: same preview, queried on the `request_id` dimension — the wallet extracts only the `request_id` from the scanned QR and re-verifies it server-side, never trusting QR contents for display; both share one `preview_oauth_consent_impl(did, query_key, query_value)` core), and `confirm_oauth_consent(did, request_id, client_id, decision, granted_scope) -> ConsentDecision` (signs the canonical `crypto::encode_oauth_consent_envelope` — server DID from `describe_server`, account DID, per-DID device key, `request_id`, `client_id`, decision, granted-scope hash, timestamp, nonce — with the DID's device key and POSTs `/oauth/authorize/approve`). Mirrors `sovereign_session.rs` exactly (per-DID key resolved before any request, `pds_url_is_safe`, DID-doc match); the frontend gates `confirmOAuthConsent` behind `authenticateBiometric()`, so a cancelled prompt signs and sends nothing. Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&PdsClient`, tested against httpmock. `ConsentError` (IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNSUPPORTED_HOST, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, APPROVAL_REJECTED, ALREADY_RESOLVED, RATE_LIMITED, TRANSPORT_FAILURE, KEYCHAIN_FAILURE, SIGNING_FAILED, DID_MISMATCH, SERVER_MISMATCH, INVALID_RESPONSE, SERVER_FAILURE) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields
- `src/app_passwords.rs` — App-password management (3 Tauri IPC commands — the "sign the official Bluesky app into a passwordless sovereign account" surface): `create_app_password(did, name, privileged) -> AppPasswordCreated` (mints via `com.atproto.server.createAppPassword`; the returned secret is surfaced ONCE — the frontend gates the call behind `authenticateBiometric()`), `list_app_passwords(did) -> Vec<AppPasswordEntry>` (metadata only), `revoke_app_password(did, name)` (server deletes the credential + its sessions/refresh tokens atomically). All three resolve a per-DID full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (the PDS routes require full access — an app password cannot manage app passwords); a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED{reason}`, the frontend's cue to run `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry, mirroring `handle_change.rs`. Thin XRPC wrappers + response types (`AppPasswordCreated`, `AppPasswordEntry`) live in `pds_client.rs`; a 409 duplicate name maps to `DUPLICATE_NAME`. `AppPasswordsError` (SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, DUPLICATE_NAME, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)
- `src/blob_backup.rs` — User-held blob backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up media" surface): `get_blob_backup_status(did)` (mirror location + opt-in flag + mirror size), `set_blob_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_blob_backup(did)` (incremental sync pass: paginated public `com.atproto.sync.listBlobs` → diff against the manifest → `getBlob` with Content-Type capture → **recompute the CIDv1 raw-codec SHA-256 CID and compare before writing** → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/blobs/{cid}` → append to the per-DID manifest `{root}/manifests/{sanitized-did}.json` (`cid, mimeType, size, fetchedAt`), saved after every blob so an interrupted run resumes; per-blob failures land in the report, never abort the run), and `restore_blob_backup(did)` (walk the manifest, re-verify each file's hash, `uploadBlob` with the stored MIME type over a `SessionProvider::full_access_client` session — `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED`, the biometric-`sovereignLogin` retry cue; an undownloaded iCloud placeholder or corrupt file is a per-blob failure with guidance). A corrupt manifest is fail-closed (`MANIFEST_CORRUPT`, file preserved — it may be the only record of MIME types for bytes the PDS has lost). `BlobBackupError` (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
