- Keychain account `"pending-removals"` stores a JSON array of DIDs whose PDS account was deleted but whose did:plc tombstone + local wipe has not yet completed (`identity_removal.rs`); written the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds and cleared once `tombstone_and_wipe` finishes, so a removal interrupted mid-tombstone is resumable on the next launch. An empty set deletes the entry; a corrupt/unreadable entry reads as empty (the marker is a best-effort safety net, never a launch blocker)
- Per-DID Keychain accounts follow the `"{did}:suffix"` pattern with ten suffixes: `device-key` (P-256 private key scalar, software path only; not written on SE path), `device-key-pub` (compressed public key, SE path only), `device-key-app-label` (SE application_label, SE path only), `did-doc` (opaque DID document JSON), `plc-log` (opaque PLC audit log JSON), `oauth-tokens` (versioned JSON containing that DID's full-access JWT pair, hosting PDS/server DID, expiry metadata, and storage timestamp), `recovery-signing-key` (the raw P-256 scalar of the self-controlled disaster-recovery `atproto` signing key, written with a read-back verify by `disaster_recovery.rs` before its enroll op is submitted), `blob-backup-enabled` (the media-backup opt-in flag, `"true"`/`"false"`; naming owned by `blob_backup::backup_enabled_account`), `repo-backup-enabled` (the post/repo-backup opt-in flag, `"true"`/`"false"`; naming owned by `repo_backup::backup_enabled_account`), `self-held-kit` (the durable "this identity carries an escrow-less kit" marker, `"true"`; naming owned by `self_held_kit::self_held_kit_account` — read only by the one-time escrow upsell seam)

- `AgentsError` variant names serialize as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE to the frontend -- the TypeScript `AgentsError.code` union in `$lib/ipc` must match exactly (NOT_AUTHENTICATED, CODE_NOT_FOUND, CODE_EXPIRED, ALREADY_CLAIMED, ACCESS_DENIED, AGENT_NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED, SESSION_LOCKED, NETWORK_ERROR, UNKNOWN); `SESSION_LOCKED` carries `reason: UnlockReason`, the cue to run `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry; the agent IPC types (`AgentSummary`, `AgentAuditEvent`, `AgentAuditPage`, `AgentClaimPreview`, `AgentClaimConfirmation`) serialize with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and their `$lib/ipc` counterparts must match exactly

The `oauth_consent_approval` step is per-identity, reached from `DIDDocumentScreen` (`onsignin`)
- `AppPasswordsError` variant names serialize as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE with camelCase fields to the frontend -- the TypeScript `AppPasswordsError` union in `$lib/ipc` must match exactly (SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, DUPLICATE_NAME, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR); `SESSION_LOCKED` carries `reason: UnlockReason`, the cue to run `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry. `SERVER_ERROR.status` is `number | null` — `Some(status)` for a classified PDS HTTP refusal, `None` for a session-lifecycle failure that isn't a transport error (unsupported host, keychain, malformed response) — `map_session_error` is exhaustive so none of those flatten into `NETWORK_ERROR`. The app-password IPC types (`AppPasswordCreated`, `AppPasswordEntry`) serialize with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and their `$lib/ipc` counterparts must match exactly; `AppPasswordCreated.password` is the one-time secret — displayed once, offered for copy, never persisted by the wallet
- `BlobBackupError` variant names serialize as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE with camelCase fields to the frontend -- the TypeScript `BlobBackupError` union in `$lib/ipc` must match exactly (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, KEYCHAIN_ERROR); `SESSION_LOCKED` carries `reason: UnlockReason` and can only come from `restore_blob_backup` (the backup pass reads public sync endpoints and needs no session). The blob-backup IPC types (`BlobBackupStatus`, `BlobBackupRunReport`, `BlobRestoreReport`, `BlobFailure`) serialize with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and their `$lib/ipc` counterparts must match exactly. The mirror's iCloud entitlements are TRACKED content: `src-tauri/Entitlements.ios.plist` is the source of truth, installed into the generated project by `ios-postinit`'s Patch H (tauri's build-time codesign reads the DEFAULT `gen/apple/<name>_iOS/<name>_iOS.entitlements` path regardless of the XcodeGen template, so the template keeps that default path and Patch H overwrites the generated file — repointing the template leaves that path fileless and signing dies with "cannot read entitlement data"). It and the `NSUbiquitousContainers` entry in `Info.ios.plist` must keep the container id `iCloud.dev.malpercio.identitywallet` in sync — `just ios-template-check` (source) and `just ios-check` (generated project's sha marker) guard both
- `RepoBackupError` variant names serialize as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE with camelCase fields to the frontend -- the TypeScript `RepoBackupError` union in `$lib/ipc` must match exactly (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR). There is deliberately **no `SESSION_LOCKED`** — repo backup reads the public `getRepo` and export reads local disk, so neither needs a session. The repo-backup IPC types (`RepoBackupStatus`, `RepoBackupRunReport`, `RepoExport`) serialize with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` and their `$lib/ipc` counterparts must match exactly. The snapshot rides the SAME iCloud ubiquity container + entitlements as the blob mirror (`repo/{sanitized-did}.{car,json}` alongside blob's `blobs/`+`manifests/`), so it needs no new entitlement, `NSUbiquitousContainers` entry, or `ios-template-check`/`ios-check` change
- Steps `my_agents` and `agent_approval` in `+page.svelte` are **per-identity**, reached from `DIDDocumentScreen` (identity detail, via `onagents`) carrying `selectedDid` — not the home list. They render `MyAgentsScreen` (the agent list for that `did`, which renders `AgentDetailScreen` — audit trail + biometric-gated revoke — on selection; a `SESSION_LOCKED` load offers a passwordless `sovereignLogin(did)` unlock) and `AgentClaimApprovalScreen` (code entry → `previewAgentClaim(did, …)` review → `authenticateBiometric` → `confirmAgentClaim(did, …)`); the biometric prompt precedes the confirm network call, so a rejected gate grants nothing
- `SignedMigrationOp` serializes with `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` -- TypeScript receives `{ diff, signedOp }`
- `MigrationState` in `AppState` uses `tokio::sync::Mutex` (same as `RecoveryState`) because migration commands hold the lock across `.await` points; it is populated by the migration orchestrator, not by `migrate.rs` itself
- `migrate::guard_migration_op` enforces a STRICT allowlist before signing: (1) `rotationKeys[0]` == device key, (2) device key is in the DID's current rotationKeys (else `WalletNotAuthorized` → orchestrator falls back to the interop path), (3) every other proposed rotation key was recommended by the destination, (4) alsoKnownAs preserved, (5) only the `atproto_pds` service is touched. This is the inverse of `claim.rs`'s guard, which forbids the very key/service changes a migration requires
- `HandleChangeError` variant names serialize as SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE to the frontend -- the TypeScript `HandleChangeError` union in `$lib/ipc` must match exactly (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, HANDLE_NOT_AVAILABLE, INVALID_HANDLE, UPDATE_HANDLE_FAILED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND); `SESSION_LOCKED` carries `reason: UnlockReason` (same set as `SessionError`), the cue for the frontend to run `sovereignLogin(did)` and retry
- `handle_change::guard_handle_change` is the THIRD strict wallet guard, the mirror image of `migrate::guard_migration_op`: before signing the change-handle op it enforces (1) device key is in the DID's current rotationKeys (else `WalletNotAuthorized`), (2) rotationKeys unchanged, (3) verificationMethods unchanged, (4) services unchanged, (5) alsoKnownAs non-empty. So **alsoKnownAs may change; rotationKeys, verificationMethods, and services must not** — the exact opposite of migration's invariant 4 (which requires alsoKnownAs preserved). The build assembles the op with every non-alsoKnownAs field passed through as current==proposed, so the guard proves the op is a pure handle change

The cache is a process-global `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<host, ServerCapabilities>>>` (unit-of-global shape, like `IdentityStore`) keyed by a trailing-slash/case-normalized host; `PdsClient::describe_server` records into it on **every** successful call, so migration prepare, handle change, consent, and sovereign login all warm it for free, and `probe()` is the cached read that describes the server only when nothing is known. **Absence is not an error** — a response with no `custos` object (every non-Custos PDS) yields `ServerCapabilities::none()`, and a failed probe yields the same **uncached** (caching it would freeze a transient outage into a permanent verdict). ## Troubleshooting

### `cargo tauri ios dev` fails with "Connection refused"

You launched the Xcode build manually (clicking Run in Xcode) instead of through `cargo tauri ios dev`. Xcode's "Build Rust Code" phase calls `cargo tauri ios xcode-script`, which connects back to the `cargo tauri ios dev` process via JSON-RPC. There is no server to connect to if the build was not initiated by `cargo tauri ios dev`.

**Fix:** Always use `cargo tauri ios dev` from the terminal. Do not click Run in Xcode.

---

### `error: can't find crate for 'core'` — `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` target not installed

The Nix `rust-default` package (used by `languages.rust` in devenv) does not ship iOS cross-compilation stdlibs. This was the historical state of the project before the rustup migration.

**Fix:** Already resolved. `devenv.nix` uses `pkgs.rustup` with project-local `RUSTUP_HOME`/`CARGO_HOME`. On first `nix develop`, `enterShell` runs `rustup toolchain install` which reads `rust-toolchain.toml` and installs `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` stdlib automatically.

If you see this after a fresh clone: make sure you entered the dev shell from the **workspace root** (not from `apps/identity-wallet/`) so that `CARGO_HOME` resolves correctly.

---

### `error: tool 'simctl' not found` or `xcrun simctl list` fails

The Nix devenv's Darwin setup hooks override `DEVELOPER_DIR` (and `SDKROOT`) to a Nix apple-sdk stub that has no runtime tools. The `xcbuild` xcrun shim in PATH delegates to `$DEVELOPER_DIR/usr/bin/xcrun` — if `DEVELOPER_DIR` points at a Nix stub, it fails.

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. `devenv.nix`'s `enterShell` sources `apps/identity-wallet/scripts/ios-env.sh`. The catch: `/usr/bin/xcode-select -p` and `/usr/bin/xcrun` both **honor `DEVELOPER_DIR` above the system Xcode selection**, so calling them by absolute path is not enough — they echo the Nix stub straight back. `ios-env.sh` first **unsets `DEVELOPER_DIR` when it points into `/nix/store`**, so `xcode-select -p` falls through to the real Xcode selection; it then re-exports `DEVELOPER_DIR` to that real path. (A genuine Xcode-provided `DEVELOPER_DIR` — not under `/nix/store` — is left untouched, so the Xcode Run Script keeps Xcode's own value.)

If you still see this: verify with `echo $DEVELOPER_DIR` inside the dev shell. If it shows a Nix store path, exit and re-enter the shell from the workspace root.

---

### `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted` (Tauri ios-api build)

Swift Package Manager sandboxes its manifest compilation using `sandbox-exec`. On macOS 26 (Tahoe), `sandbox_apply()` returns `EPERM` in this context, causing `swift-rs`'s build script (used by Tauri) to fail with "Failed to compile swift package Tauri".

**Fix:** Already resolved and applied automatically. A local patch of `swift-rs` 1.0.7 at `apps/identity-wallet/swift-rs-patch/` adds `--disable-sandbox` to the `swift build` invocation inside `SwiftLinker::link`. The workspace `Cargo.toml` wires this in via `[patch.crates-io]`. See `docs/ios-upstream-bugs.md` for details. Remove the patch entry when swift-rs ships a fix upstream.

---

### `Failed to update the excludes stack to see if a path is excluded` (Xcode user script sandbox)

Xcode 14+ enables `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING=YES` by default in generated projects, wrapping Run Script build phases in `sandbox-exec`. On macOS 26 (Tahoe), this sandbox blocks Cargo's `readdir()` calls during package fingerprinting, producing:

```
error: failed to determine package fingerprint for build script for identity-wallet v0.1.0
Caused by: Failed to update the excludes stack to see if a path is excluded
```

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. The `scripts/ios/project.yml` template sets `ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING: NO`, which every `cargo tauri ios init` renders into the generated project; `just ios-check` verifies the setting is in place.

---

### `Undefined symbols ... _SC*` / `_ASWebAuthenticationSession*` — an Apple framework not linked at `Ld`

The Rust code compiles, then Xcode's link step fails with `Undefined symbols for architecture arm64:` naming Apple framework symbols — e.g. `_SCDynamicStore...` / `_SCNetworkReachability...` (Apple's `SystemConfiguration.framework`, which the `system-configuration` crate needs — pulled in transitively by `hickory-resolver` for system DNS config and `reqwest` for system proxy detection), or `_ASWebAuthenticationSessionErrorDomain` (Apple's `AuthenticationServices.framework`, which the vendored `tauri-plugin-auth-session` needs via `objc2-authentication-services` / `ASWebAuthenticationSession`).

Host builds (`cargo test` / `cargo build`) link fine because **rustc** does the final link and honors the crate's `#[link(name = "...", kind = "framework")]`. On iOS the crate is built as a `staticlib` (`libapp.a`) and **Xcode** does the final link — it never sees that embedded directive, so the framework must be declared in the Xcode project or the symbols stay undefined. A `build.rs` `cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework=...` does NOT help (same staticlib → Xcode gap).

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. The `scripts/ios/project.yml` template renders `OTHER_LDFLAGS = "$(inherited) -framework SystemConfiguration -framework AuthenticationServices"` from `bundle > iOS > frameworks` in `tauri.conf.json` (the same list also produces xcodegen `sdk:` link dependencies), and `just ios-check` verifies every listed framework. The historical footgun this design removes: `bundle.iOS.frameworks` used to seed only a FRESH project.yml, because `cargo tauri ios init` preserves an existing one — with the custom template, project.yml is re-rendered from config on every init, so the config is now the enforced mechanism. To link another Apple framework a new Rust dep requires, **add it to `bundle > iOS > frameworks` in `tauri.conf.json`** and re-run `cargo tauri ios init` + `just ios-postinit` — never hand-edit `OTHER_LDFLAGS` in the generated project (a second `OTHER_LDFLAGS` assignment for the same build config shadows, not appends to, the first, silently dropping a framework — `just ios-check` detects that state).

---

### `libapp.a ... is not permitted` / `Invalid bundle structure` on TestFlight upload

`cargo tauri ios build` succeeds and `xcrun altool` then rejects the upload (HTTP 409): *"The 'Obsign.app/libapp.a' binary file is not permitted. Your app cannot contain standalone executables or libraries."* (tauri#13578.)

cargo-mobile2 lists the `Externals` directory (which holds the Rust staticlib `libapp.a`) as a project source with **no explicit `buildPhase`**, so XcodeGen infers `resources` and copies the raw `.a` into the `.app` — which App Store validation forbids. The library is also (correctly) **linked** via the separate `framework: libapp.a` entry + `LIBRARY_SEARCH_PATHS`, so excluding it from resources is safe.

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. The `scripts/ios/project.yml` template sets `Externals → buildPhase: none`, so xcodegen never emits a `libapp.a in Resources` entry (the `framework: libapp.a` link dependency is kept). `just ios-check` verifies both layers.

---

### `base64: invalid option -- 'o'` during `cargo tauri ios build` signing

The build reads `IOS_CERTIFICATE` and fails decoding it: `base64: invalid option -- 'o'`. In the Nix dev shell, GNU coreutils `base64` shadows macOS's BSD `base64` in `PATH`, but Tauri's cert decode uses BSD-only flags (`-i`/`-o`). (CI is unaffected — the runner has no Nix.)

**Fix:** Already resolved automatically. `scripts/ios-env.sh` (under `EZPDS_IOS_BUILD=1`) shims `/usr/bin/base64` ahead of the Nix one via a tiny symlink dir on `PATH` — surgical (only `base64`), leaving every other Nix tool untouched.

I'm seeing a clear refactoring pattern here: consolidate all the unlock calls by creating a new `unlockIdentity` function that handles the logic centrally. This function would check with the backend to determine which authentication method the host supports, then route to either the sovereign login flow or trigger a password-based UI modal. Since these unlock calls are scattered throughout async code, wrapping the modal in a promise makes sense for maintaining the async flow.

For Svelte 5, I'd use a module-level store to track pending password unlock requests and render a shared `<PasswordUnlockDialog />` once in the root page, which resolves the promise when the user completes authentication. This keeps the implementation clean and minimizes changes across screens—just swapping one import.

The implementation approach is to create a handler registration system where the dialog component registers itself as the password prompt handler, keeping the unlock module pure and testable rather than relying on Svelte runes in a `.svelte.ts` file.

The backend returns unlock method info including whether the identity is sovereign or password-protected, along with the PDS URL and an optional identifier suggestion (pulled from the DID document's alsoKnownAs field) to prefill the login form. If the capability probe can't reach the host, it safely degrades to password authentication.

For offline scenarios, I'm thinking we should prefer the SOVEREIGN method when the network is unreachable rather than prompting for a password that will fail anyway — this aligns with the design principle of keeping Custos identities unchanged. content.text:
Now I have the full picture. Let me start with the backend.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The provider's ladder reads a **persisted record**, not a login method — so a password `createSession` can light up every downstream feature by writing the same `{did}:oauth-tokens` shape that `sovereignLogin` writes. No change to `session_provider.rs` at all, which is exactly what AC 3 demands.
- `source_login.rs` currently hands back an `OAuthClient`, which swallows the raw JWTs. To persist them I need to split its core: the `createSession` + error-mapping + account-match guard becomes reusable, and the Bearer-client construction becomes the thin wrapper the two existing callers keep.
- Capability probing has a subtlety already encoded in `pds_capabilities`: `reached: false` means *we could not ask*, not *no sovereign sessions*. Routing an offline Custos identity to a password prompt would be a lie, so unreached must fall back to the sovereign path.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

<script lang="ts">
  import type { Snippet } from 'svelte';
  import { isCodedError } from '$lib/ipc';
  import { formatRateLimitMessage, formatServerErrorMessage } from '$lib/claim-errors';
  import OnboardingShell from '$lib/components/ui/OnboardingShell.svelte';
  import TextField from '$lib/components/ui/TextField.svelte';
  import Button from '$lib/components/ui/Button.svelte';
  import Spinner from '$lib/components/ui/Spinner.svelte';

  // Shared base for the two wallet source-PDS password logins — the claim flow (`PdsAuthScreen`)
  // and the outbound migration (`MigrationSourceAuthScreen`). Both open a full session against the
  // account's current PDS with a password `createSession` and are ~identical bar copy, the IPC fn,
  // and a handful of error codes. This component owns the form, the 2FA branch, and the
  // shared error switch; each wrapper supplies its copy, its `authenticate` IPC fn, and a mapper
  // for the codes only it produces.

  // The shape every source-login error enum serializes to (`ClaimError` / `MigrationError`): a
  // SCREAMING_SNAKE `code`, plus an optional `message`/`retryAfter` on some variants.
  type CodedAuthError = { code: string; message?: string; retryAfter?: string | null };

  let {
    did,
    handle,
    pdsUrl,
    onnext,
    onback,
    authenticate,
    errorLogLabel,
    openingStatus,
    title,
    subtitle,
    why,
    appPasswordClause,
    mapExtraError,
  }: {
    did: string;
    handle: string;
    pdsUrl: string;
    onnext: () => void;
    onback: () => void;
    /** IPC source-login command: one-shot password `createSession` against the source PDS. */
    authenticate: (
      did: string,
      identifier: string,
      password: string,
      twoFactorToken?: string,
    ) => Promise<void>;
    /** `console.error` label for a failed sign-in (per-flow, aids log triage). */
    errorLogLabel: string;
    /** Status line under the spinner while the session opens. */
    openingStatus: string;
    /** Main (non-2FA) form title. */
    title: string;
    /** Main (non-2FA) form subtitle. */
    subtitle: string;
    /** The rich "why a full password sign-in" explainer for the main form. */
    why: Snippet;
    /**
     * Trailing clause of the `SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED` message: the shared sentence structure lives here
     * to stop the two copies drifting (the exact hazard duplication created here); only this clause varies
     * — e.g. "authorize the move" vs "authorize identity changes".
     */
    appPasswordClause: string;
    /**
     * Map a flow-specific error code (one the shared switch below doesn't handle) to a message.
     * Return `null` to fall through to the generic "Sign-in failed (CODE)" default.
     */
    mapExtraError: (code: string) => string | null;
  } = $props();

  // Prefill the login identifier with the handle, then let the user edit it to a DID or email if
  // that is how they sign in to their PDS. Capturing the initial value is intentional — this
  // screen's `handle` prop is fixed for its lifetime, so it never needs to re-sync.
  // svelte-ignore state_referenced_locally
  let identifier = $state(handle);
  let password = $state('');
  // For accounts with email 2FA: once the PDS asks for a code, we keep the password in memory and
  // re-submit it alongside the code the user enters here.
  let needsTwoFactor = $state(false);
  let twoFactorToken = $state('');
  let authenticating = $state(false);
  let error = $state<string | null>(null);

  async function runAuth() {
    if (!identifier.trim() || !password) return;
    if (needsTwoFactor && !twoFactorToken.trim()) return;
    authenticating = true;
    error = null;

    try {
      await authenticate(
        did,
        identifier.trim(),
        password,
        needsTwoFactor ? twoFactorToken.trim() : undefined,
      );
      // Credentials are not retained after this call resolves.
      password = '';
      twoFactorToken = '';
      onnext();
    } catch (raw: unknown) {
      authenticating = false;
      console.error(errorLogLabel, raw);

      if (isCodedError(raw)) {
        const err = raw as CodedAuthError;
        switch (err.code) {
          case 'TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED':
            if (needsTwoFactor) {
              // We already submitted a code and it wasn't accepted.
              error = "That code wasn't accepted. Check the latest code emailed to you.";
            } else {
              // First time: the account has 2FA. Advance to the code step — not an error.
              needsTwoFactor = true;
            }
            break;
          case 'SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED':
            error = needsTwoFactor
              ? "That code wasn't accepted. Check the latest code emailed to you."
              : `${pdsUrl} did not accept that password. Use your account password — an app password can't ${appPasswordClause}.`;

content.content: A recovery key for identities hosted anywhere. Until now, the wallet's Shamir recovery seed came bundled with Custos escrow, so an identity you imported from bsky.social or any other spec-compliant PDS got a Secure-Enclave root key, monitoring, and backups — but no way back in if you lost the device. The new "Add a recovery key" flow on the identity screen is the same ceremony minus the escrow: the wallet generates the seed, splits it 2-of-3, and publishes a device-key-signed operation that inserts the derived recovery key straight after your device key. Nothing is removed, and no share — nor any part of the recovery key — is ever sent to your PDS; the only thing the wallet asks it is the public question of whether it offers recovery escrow at all. Share 1 goes to your Keychain to sync across your Apple devices; Shares 2 and 3 are both yours to save, and any two of the three restore the identity through the existing recovery ceremony. The flow is offered only where it is the right answer: on a server that advertises recovery escrow, the escrow-backed upgrade is offered instead, and on a server that could not be reached nothing is offered at all rather than guessing. If you later move to a host that does hold shares, the wallet offers escrow once — as an option, not a reminder.

input.content: App passwords, handle changes, identity removal, and media restore now work on any server. Four features that are pure standard AT Protocol have been dark for identities hosted anywhere but Custos, for a single reason: each needs a full sign-in, and the only sign-in the wallet knew how to perform was the passwordless one that a Custos server offers. On bsky.social or the reference PDS there was no such option, so the buttons were there and the session behind them was not. The wallet now asks the identity's server which sign-in it supports and offers the right one: a Face ID unlock where the server accepts a device-key signature, and a prompt for your account password where it does not — with emailed two-factor codes handled, and the password sent once, to your own server, and never stored. From then on the session behaves identically either way: it refreshes on its own, and it is discarded if your identity moves to a different host. A server the wallet could not reach is never assumed to lack passwordless sign-in — it keeps offering the unlock it already used, because a network hiccup is not a fact about your server.

The `pub(crate)` JWT/audience helpers (`bearer_jwt_claims`, `audience_matches_server`) are the single source of the sub/aud binding check, reused by `session_provider`.

- `src/session_provider.rs` — per-DID full-access **session lifecycle** (the seam every authenticated Custos-hosted operation goes through; the minimum contract). `SessionProvider::full_access_client(pds_client, store, did, now) -> Result<ActiveSession, SessionError>` runs a decision ladder under a per-DID coalescing lock: (1) no record / dead refresh → `NeedsUnlock{NoRefreshChain}`; (2) access JWT still valid (`exp > now + 120s`) → rebuild a Bearer client **with no network** (this is what makes a restart or offline launch with a live token need no prompt); (3) near-expiry with a live refresh → discover the DID's current PDS, and if the host moved **discard the old-audience record** + `NeedsUnlock{HostChanged}`, else call `com.atproto.server.refreshSession` exactly once and atomically persist the rotated pair (re-validating sub/aud). - `src/plc_monitor.rs` — PLC monitoring module: `PlcMonitor` (borrows `PdsClient`; `check_all()` iterates all managed DIDs, `check_for_changes(did)` diffs current audit log against cached log and classifies new entries as authorized/unauthorized by verifying signatures against the device key); `run_monitoring_loop(app_handle)` (spawned once at app startup, checks every 15 minutes via `tokio::time::interval` with `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`, emits `"plc_alert"` Tauri event to frontend when unauthorized changes detected); `check_identity_status` (Tauri IPC command: synchronous foreground check of all managed identities, returns `Vec<IdentityStatus>`). Types: `UnauthorizedChange` { cid, created_at, signing_key, operation } (camelCase serialization), `IdentityStatus` { did, alert_count, unauthorized_changes } (camelCase serialization), `MonitorError` { NetworkError, IdentityStoreError, ParseError } (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE tag serialization)

- `src/agents.rs` — Agent consent + audit module (5 **per-identity** Tauri IPC commands, the wallet side of the auth.md claim ceremony + "My agents"): `preview_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimPreview` (POST `/v1/agents/claim-preview` — what approving would grant, shown before the biometric gate), `confirm_agent_claim(did, user_code) -> AgentClaimConfirmation` (POST `/agent/identity/claim/confirm` — the human gate; the frontend wraps it in `authenticateBiometric()`), `list_agents(did) -> Vec<AgentSummary>`, `revoke_agent(did, registration_id)`, `get_agent_audit(did, registration_id, cursor?) -> AgentAuditPage`. 111:- `src/sovereign_session.rs` — per-DID Custos sovereign login: discovers the selected DID's current PDS and server DID, signs the shared canonical envelope with that DID's device key, validates the response DID and JWT subject/audience, persists a versioned `SovereignTokenRecord`, and exposes `stored_bearer_client(did)` for authenticated XRPC helpers. `sovereign_login` is the narrow Tauri command; the typed frontend `sovereignLogin(did)` wrapper performs the biometric gate before invoking it. The `pub(crate)` JWT/audience helpers (`bearer_jwt_claims`, `audience_matches_server`) are the single source of the sub/aud binding check, reused by `session_provider`.
119:- `src/blob_backup.rs` — User-held blob backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up media" surface): `get_blob_backup_status(did)` (mirror location + opt-in flag + mirror size), `set_blob_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_blob_backup(did)` (incremental sync pass: paginated public `com.atproto.sync.listBlobs` → diff against the manifest → `getBlob` with Content-Type capture → **recompute the CIDv1 raw-codec SHA-256 CID and compare before writing** → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/blobs/{cid}` → append to the per-DID manifest `{root}/manifests/{sanitized-did}.json` (`cid, mimeType, size, fetchedAt`), saved after every blob so an interrupted run resumes; per-blob failures land in the report, never abort the run), and `restore_blob_backup(did)` (walk the manifest, re-verify each file's hash, `uploadBlob` with the stored MIME type over a `SessionProvider::full_access_client` session — `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED`, the biometric-`sovereignLogin` retry cue; an undownloaded iCloud placeholder or corrupt file is a per-blob failure with guidance). The mirror root resolves: `EZPDS_BLOB_BACKUP_DIR` env override (tests/dev) → the iCloud Drive ubiquity container `Documents/` on iOS (`NSFileManager.URLForUbiquityContainerIdentifier` via `objc2-foundation`, iOS-only target dep; user-visible in the Files app) → on a real device with iCloud off, `BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE` (never a silent local fallback) → elsewhere (macOS/simulator) a local app-data dir reported as `location: "local"`. A corrupt manifest is fail-closed (`MANIFEST_CORRUPT`, file preserved — it may be the only record of MIME types for bytes the PDS has lost). `BlobBackupError` (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)
123:- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (5 Tauri IPC commands): `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `sovereignLogin` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad password/code is `InvalidToken` with nothing mutated — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `retire_and_wipe`), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: retire + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent; for a did:web there is no tombstone to retry, so the resume is the local wipe alone), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `retire_and_wipe` completes — including on the did:web path, which is what keeps an interrupted did:web removal from becoming permanent retry state. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist and are method-agnostic, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). Types: `RemovalOutcome` { tombstoneCid (null when the removed DID has no tombstone leg — a did:web), wasLastIdentity }, `RemovalError` (SESSION_REQUIRED, REQUEST_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_TOKEN, ACCOUNT_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, TOMBSTONE_SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, LOCAL_WIPE_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR)

135:- `src/session_provider.rs::ensure_identity_session(did: String) -> Result<SessionReady, SessionError>` — Tauri IPC command: the frontend pre-flight. Restores or rotates the DID's session and reports status (dropping the in-Rust client); a `NEEDS_UNLOCK` error is the cue for the UI to offer the passwordless `sovereignLogin(did)`. Performs **no** biometric prompt — a live token must never demand one. Frontend wrapper: `ensureIdentitySession(did)`.
482:- Steps `my_agents` and `agent_approval` in `+page.svelte` are **per-identity**, reached from `DIDDocumentScreen` (identity detail, via `onagents`) carrying `selectedDid` — not the home list. They render `MyAgentsScreen` (the agent list for that `did`, which renders `AgentDetailScreen` — audit trail + biometric-gated revoke — on selection; a `SESSION_LOCKED` load offers a passwordless `sovereignLogin(did)` unlock) and `AgentClaimApprovalScreen` (code entry → `previewAgentClaim(did, …)` review → `authenticateBiometric` → `confirmAgentClaim(did, …)`); the biometric prompt precedes the confirm network call, so a rejected gate grants nothing

531:- `src/lib/ipc/` -- Per-domain typed TypeScript wrappers for all Tauri IPC commands, split into `account.ts`, `oauth.ts`, `appearance.ts`, `diagnostics.ts`, `claim.ts`, `identity.ts`, `password-unlock.ts`, `monitor.ts`, `recovery.ts`, `migration.ts`, `handle-change.ts`, `agents.ts`, `app-passwords.ts`, `blob-backup.ts`, `repo-backup.ts`, `self-held-kit.ts` (plus the generic `isCodedError` IPC-error guard in `errors.ts`), all re-exported from `index.ts`; page components import from `$lib/ipc`
534:- `src/lib/unlock.ts` -- `unlockIdentity(did, route?)`: the single place a locked identity is reopened. Asks `getIdentityUnlockRoute` which sign-in the identity's *current* host serves, then runs the biometric `sovereignLogin(did)` or hands a `PasswordUnlockRequest` to the app-level dialog and awaits the user's answer. A policy gate over IPC wrappers rather than an `invoke()` wrapper, so it sits outside `$lib/ipc` alongside `biometric.ts`. The dialog is inverted in (`registerPasswordUnlockPrompt`, returning an unregister for teardown) precisely because `unlockIdentity` is called from the middle of async operations (`catch SESSION_LOCKED → unlock → retry`) that cannot render a form of their own. A dismissed prompt rejects with `UNLOCK_CANCELLED` (`isUnlockCancelled`) — a decision, not a fault, which every screen's `messageFor` maps to `null` so cancelling renders no error. Tested by `unlock.test.ts`
535:- `src/lib/components/home/PasswordUnlockDialog.svelte` -- the app-level password unlock sheet, mounted once by `+page.svelte` above every step and rendering nothing until `$lib/unlock` needs a password. Names the host, prefills the identifier from the DID document, branches to the emailed two-factor code on `TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED` (an advance, not an error), and clears every credential it held before it closes

1	// pattern: Imperative Shell
2	//
3	// Gathers: the identity's current hosting PDS, that host's advertised capabilities,
4	//          and (for the password path) the account's one-shot password
5	// Processes: decides which unlock a host can serve, then mints a full session with
6	//            `com.atproto.server.createSession` and binds the returned pair to this DID + host
7	// Returns: the unlock route a screen should offer, or a persisted, ready session summary
8	
9	//! The second resolution of [`crate::session_provider::SessionError::NeedsUnlock`].
10	//!
11	//! Every authenticated wallet operation goes through
12	//! [`SessionProvider::full_access_client`](crate::session_provider::SessionProvider::full_access_client),
13	//! which resolves a session from the DID's persisted `{did}:oauth-tokens` record. Until now
14	//! that record had exactly one origin: the biometric, passwordless
15	//! [`sovereign_login`](crate::sovereign_session::sovereign_login), which only a host
16	//! advertising `sovereignSessions` can serve. So a claimed identity hosted on bsky.social or
17	//! the reference PDS had no way to obtain one, and every feature built on that seam — app
18	//! passwords, change handle, identity removal, blob restore — was dark for it despite being
19	//! pure standard lexicon.
20	//!
21	//! This module supplies the missing origin. A password `createSession` (the machinery
22	//! [`crate::source_login`] already runs transiently for the claim and migration source logins)
23	//! produces the same full-access JWT pair, which is persisted into the **same** versioned
24	//! record. From that write on, the provider's ladder — restore, rotate via `refreshSession`,
25	//! discard on host change — owns the session and behaves identically regardless of which
26	//! unlock minted it. Nothing in `session_provider.rs` changes.
27	//!
28	//! Two postures carry over from the claim flow unchanged: the full session is required
29	//! because a `transition:generic` OAuth token cannot drive identity operations (ADR-0021),
30	//! and the password is used for exactly one request and never stored.
31	
32	use serde::Serialize;
33	
34	use crate::identity_store::{IdentityStore, IdentityStoreError, SovereignTokenRecord};
35	use crate::pds_client::{PdsClient, PdsClientError};
36	use crate::session_provider::SessionReady;
37	use crate::source_login::{create_source_session, SourceLoginError};
38	use crate::sovereign_session::{audience_matches_server, bearer_jwt_claims};
39	
40	/// How a given identity's host can turn a locked identity back into a live session.
41	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
42	#[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]
43	pub enum UnlockMethod {
44	    /// The host advertises `sovereignSessions`: a device-key proof mints the session with no
45	    /// password, behind the biometric gate.
46	    Sovereign,
47	    /// The host serves only the standard lexicon: the account's password opens the session.
48	    Password,
49	}
50	
51	/// Which unlock a screen should offer for one identity, plus what the prompt needs to say.
52	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
53	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
54	pub struct UnlockRoute {
55	    pub method: UnlockMethod,
56	    /// The identity's current hosting PDS — named in the password prompt so the user knows
57	    /// whose password is being asked for.
58	    pub pds_url: String,
59	    /// The account's handle from its DID document, offered as the prefilled `identifier`.
60	    /// `None` when the document carries no `at://` alias; the DID itself is then the fallback
61	    /// identifier, which `createSession` accepts.
62	    pub handle: Option<String>,
63	}
64	
65	/// Why a password unlock could not produce a session.
66	///
67	/// Serializes as `{ "code": "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE", ... }` alongside `SessionError` /
68	/// `ClaimError` / `MigrationError`. The credential-shaped variants mirror the claim flow's,
69	/// because they are the same `createSession` failures seen from a different screen.
70	#[derive(Debug, Serialize, thiserror::Error)]
71	#[serde(
72	    tag = "code",
73	    rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE",
74	    rename_all_fields = "camelCase"
75	)]
76	pub enum UnlockError {
77	    #[error("identity not found")]
78	    IdentityNotFound,
79	    #[error("the identity's hosting server could not be resolved")]
80	    UnsupportedHost,
81	    /// The account has email two-factor enabled; the host has emailed a code and the caller
82	    /// re-invokes with `auth_factor_token`.
83	    #[error("a two-factor code is required")]
84	    TwoFactorRequired,
85	    #[error("the hosting server did not accept that password")]
86	    InvalidCredentials { message: String },
87	    /// The credentials signed in to a different account than the one being unlocked.
88	    #[error("those credentials are for a different account")]
89	    AccountMismatch,
90	    /// The hosting endpoint from the DID document is not HTTPS, so the password is refused
91	    /// rather than sent in cleartext.
92	    #[error("the hosting server's endpoint is not secure")]
93	    InsecureHostUrl,
94	    #[error("the hosting server rate limited the sign-in")]
95	    RateLimited { retry_after: Option<String> },
96	    #[error("hosting server failure: {message}")]
97	    ServerError { message: String },
98	    #[error("offline or transport failure: {message}")]
99	    NetworkError { message: String },
100	    #[error("keychain failure: {message}")]
101	    Keychain { message: String },
102	    #[error("invalid session response: {message}")]
103	    InvalidResponse { message: String },
104	}
105	
106	impl From<SourceLoginError> for UnlockError {
107	    fn from(error: SourceLoginError) -> Self {
108	        match error {
109	            SourceLoginError::TwoFactorRequired => Self::TwoFactorRequired,
110	            SourceLoginError::SourceAuthFailed { message } => Self::InvalidCredentials { message },
111	            SourceLoginError::AccountMismatch => Self::AccountMismatch,
112	            SourceLoginError::InsecureSourceUrl => Self::InsecureHostUrl,
113	            SourceLoginError::RateLimited { retry_after } => Self::RateLimited { retry_after },
114	            SourceLoginError::ServerError { message } => Self::ServerError { message },
115	            SourceLoginError::NetworkError { message } => Self::NetworkError { message },
116	        }
117	    }
118	}
119	
120	fn map_store_error(error: IdentityStoreError) -> UnlockError {
121	    match error {
122	        IdentityStoreError::IdentityNotFound => UnlockError::IdentityNotFound,
123	        IdentityStoreError::KeychainError { message } => UnlockError::Keychain { message },
124	        other => UnlockError::Keychain {
125	            message: other.to_string(),
126	        },
127	    }
128	}
129	
130	/// Map a DID-discovery failure. A transport failure is a connectivity problem; anything that
131	/// means the DID or its PDS metadata could not be read leaves us with no host to sign in to.
132	fn map_discovery_error(error: PdsClientError) -> UnlockError {
133	    match error {
134	        PdsClientError::PdsUnreachable { reason } => UnlockError::NetworkError { message: reason },
135	        PdsClientError::NetworkError { message } => UnlockError::NetworkError { message },
136	        PdsClientError::RateLimited { retry_after, .. } => UnlockError::RateLimited { retry_after },
137	        other => {
138	            tracing::warn!(error = %other, "could not resolve the identity's hosting server");
139	            UnlockError::UnsupportedHost
140	        }
141	    }
142	}
143	
144	/// The account's handle from its DID document's first `at://` alias.
145	fn handle_from_also_known_as(also_known_as: &[String]) -> Option<String> {
146	    also_known_as
147	        .iter()
148	        .find_map(|alias| alias.strip_prefix("at://"))
149	        .map(str::to_string)
150	}

identically regardless of which unlock minted the session, which a test proves
by restoring a password-minted session through the provider with an unroutable
plc.directory.

Closes [MM-457](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-457) — Phase 2 of [MM-452](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-452) (Obsign without Custos). Design: `docs/design-plans/2026-07-24-obsign-without-custos.md` §Phase 2.

## The problem

App passwords, change handle, identity removal, and blob restore are built entirely on standard AT Protocol lexicons — nothing about them needs Custos. They were dark for a claimed identity on bsky.social or the reference PDS for one narrow reason: each goes through `SessionProvider::full_access_client`, whose `NeedsUnlock` had exactly one resolution — the biometric, passwordless `sovereignLogin`, which only a host advertising `sovereignSessions` can serve. The buttons were there; the session behind them was not.

## The change

`session_provider.rs` is **untouched**. The insight is that the provider's ladder reads a *persisted record*, not a login method — so a second origin for that record lights up everything downstream for free.

**`password_unlock.rs`** (new, 2 commands):
- `get_identity_unlock_route(did) -> { method, pdsUrl, handle }` — discovers the DID's current host, reads `pds_capabilities::probe`, answers `SOVEREIGN` or `PASSWORD`.
- `unlock_identity_with_password(did, identifier, password, authFactorToken?)` — password `createSession`, validates the pair's `sub`/`aud` against this DID + host, persists a `SovereignTokenRecord` into the **same** `{did}:oauth-tokens` slot `sovereignLogin` writes.

A test proves the seam rather than the plumbing: it mints a session by password, then restores it through `SessionProvider::full_access_client` with an **unroutable** plc.directory. No network, no prompt — the record shape is provably the one the existing ladder understands.

**An unreached capability probe routes to `SOVEREIGN`, not `PASSWORD`.** `reached: false` means the question could not be put to the host. Demanding a password on that basis would both misstate a fact about the user's server and change behavior for every Custos identity whose launch happens to be offline.

**`source_login.rs`** gains `create_source_session` — the `createSession` half returning the raw JWT pair, since an `OAuthClient` deliberately does not surrender its tokens. `authenticate_source_password` is now a thin wrapper over it, so the HTTPS-only, one-shot-password, and account-match guards stay on every source-login path with one implementation and one test suite.

**Frontend.** `$lib/unlock`'s `unlockIdentity(did)` replaces the inline `sovereignLogin(did)` in all four screens and owns the branch, so no screen decides for itself which sign-in its host supports. The password form is an app-level dialog registered *into* that module — inverted because `unlockIdentity` is called from inside async operations (`catch SESSION_LOCKED → unlock → retry`) that cannot render a form of their own.

Email 2FA advances the form rather than reading as a wrong password. A dismissed prompt rejects with `UNLOCK_CANCELLED`, which each screen's `messageFor` maps to `null` — cancelling is a decision, not a fault, so it renders no error.

`unlock_identity_with_password` is deliberately **not** biometric-gated: the password is itself the presence proof and nothing is device-key-signed. The irreversible operations it unlocks keep their own gates, exactly as after a sovereign unlock. ADR-0021 holds, and the password is sent once and never stored.

## Acceptance criteria

1. ✅ Four features reachable on a foreign host, behind the same biometric gates as the Custos paths.
2. ✅ Unlock branches on host capability, with 2FA handled — verified in the browser harness (below).
3. ✅ `session_provider.rs` unchanged; all 662 wallet Rust tests pass, every `session_provider` test included.

## Verification

Driven in the browser harness (`self-held-kit` scenario — a claimed identity on `bsky.social` whose host advertises nothing) with `failNext('list_app_passwords', { code: 'SESSION_LOCKED' })`:

- Locked App Passwords → **Unlock** → the password sheet appears, naming `https://bsky.social`, identifier prefilled from the DID document, password field focused.
- `failNext('unlock_identity_with_password', { code: 'TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED' })` → the sheet advances to the emailed-code step with no error shown.
- Entering the code → unlock succeeds → the original app-password load retries and renders.
- Switching to the `one-identity` (Custos) scenario and repeating: **no dialog** — the sovereign route is taken, unchanged.

Gates run: `cargo test -p identity-wallet` (662 passed), `cargo clippy -p identity-wallet --all-targets -D warnings`, `rustfmt`, `pnpm check` (0 errors), `pnpm test` (170 passed, 6 new in `unlock.test.ts`), `just ticket-ref-check`, `just changelog-check`, `just docs-check` (IPC reference regenerated).

## Notes for review

- No PDS/server changes and no new routes, so no Bruno collection changes.
- The shared `{did}:oauth-tokens` record shape is now written by two paths; a change to `SovereignTokenRecord` must keep both writers and the provider's reader in step. Noted as an invariant in the wallet's AGENTS.md.

Done. [PR #451](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/451) is open; MM-457 is In Review with the PR attached.

## What shipped

**Backend** — [password_unlock.rs](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/password_unlock.rs), two commands: `get_identity_unlock_route` (capability-driven `SOVEREIGN` vs `PASSWORD`) and `unlock_identity_with_password` (password `createSession` → `sub`/`aud` binding check → persist into the same `{did}:oauth-tokens` record). [session_provider.rs](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/session_provider.rs) is untouched. [source_login.rs](apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/source_login.rs) split so `create_source_session` returns the raw JWT pair while keeping the HTTPS / one-shot / account-match guards on every path.

**Frontend** — [unlock.ts](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/unlock.ts) owns the branch; [PasswordUnlockDialog.svelte](apps/identity-wallet/src/lib/components/home/PasswordUnlockDialog.svelte) is the app-level prompt; the four screens each swapped one call.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **The seam was the whole design.** Because the provider resolves from a *persisted record* rather than a login method, adding a second way to write that record lit up four features without touching the thing that consumes it. That's why AC 3 was free rather than fought for — and why the test that matters restores a password-minted session through the provider against an unroutable plc.directory.
- **Inverting the dialog is what made the screens a one-line change.** `unlockIdentity` gets called from inside `catch SESSION_LOCKED → unlock → retry`, which has no way to render a form. Registering the prompt into the module and resolving a promise means the call site keeps its exact shape whether the answer is a fingerprint or a typed password.
- **`reached: false` is not a fact about the server.** The codebase already encoded that distinction in `pds_capabilities`; the new gate had to honor it, or a Custos user opening the app on a flaky connection would suddenly be asked for a password their server never wanted.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Two things worth flagging:

- **The record shape is now written by two paths.** A change to `SovereignTokenRecord` must keep `sovereign_session`, `password_unlock`, and the provider's reader in step. I recorded that as an invariant in the wallet's AGENTS.md, but it's the sharpest edge this PR introduces.
- **Verification was harness-only.** I drove the real flow in the browser (foreign host → prompt → 2FA → success → retry; Custos → no prompt), which covers AC 2 honestly. What it can't cover is a live `createSession` against actual bsky.social, and the Keychain/biometric layer. AC 1's "a claimed bsky.social identity can…" deserves an on-device pass before you call it validated.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/pr-review-comments

# Batch PR Review-Comment Triage

Pull every unresolved review thread on the current PR in one command, then triage the batch. The user should never have to paste review comments one at a time.

## Fetch unresolved threads

Determine the PR number for the current branch (`gh pr view --json number -q .number`), then:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){
    pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){
        nodes{
          isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:30){nodes{author{login} body url}}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}' -F owner=<owner> -F repo=<repo> -F pr=<number> \
| jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
       | select(.isResolved==false)
       | {path, line, isOutdated,
          comments: [.comments.nodes[] | {author: .author.login, url, body}]}]'
```

Also fetch top-level (non-thread) review bodies and issue comments if the bot posts summaries there:

```bash
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments
```

## Triage the batch

For each unresolved thread, classify before fixing anything:

1. **Correctness / security / portability** — verify the claim against the actual code, then fix if real. Automated reviewers assert confidently and are sometimes wrong; refute with evidence when they are.
2. **Legitimate but out of scope** — file a follow-up issue rather than growing the PR.
3. **Pure style nit / preference** — decline with a one-line reason.

Present the full disposition table (thread → classification → action) to the user in ONE message before applying fixes, so they approve the batch rather than each item. Note that every fix-commit re-triggers CI and (for assertive bots like CodeRabbit) a fresh review round that tends to find one more micro-nit — batch fixes into a single commit where possible.

## Resolving threads

After pushing fixes, reply/resolve via:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=<threadId>
```

(Include `id` in the reviewThreads query above if you plan to resolve threads programmatically.)

  import { onMount, tick } from 'svelte';

  import { isCodedError, unlockIdentityWithPassword, type UnlockError } from '$lib/ipc';
  import { formatRateLimitMessage, formatServerErrorMessage } from '$lib/claim-errors';
  import {
    registerPasswordUnlockPrompt,
    UNLOCK_CANCELLED,
    type PasswordUnlockRequest,
  } from '$lib/unlock';
  import Button from '$lib/components/ui/Button.svelte';
  import Spinner from '$lib/components/ui/Spinner.svelte';
  import TextField from '$lib/components/ui/TextField.svelte';

  // The app-level password unlock prompt: mounted once at the root, driven by `$lib/unlock`.
  //
  // A Custos-hosted identity reopens with a device-key signature and no dialog at all. On any
  // other spec-compliant host there is no such proof, so the account's password opens the
  // session (ADR-0021 — the operations behind it need a full session, which no OAuth
  // `transition:generic` token can grant). The password is submitted once and never stored:
  // only the JWT pair the server returns is persisted, into the same record `sovereignLogin`
  // writes.
  //
  // It lives at the root rather than inside each screen because `unlockIdentity` is called from
  // the middle of async operations (`catch SESSION_LOCKED → unlock → retry`), which cannot
  // render a form of their own. The dialog resolves the promise those callers are awaiting.

  type Pending = {
    request: PasswordUnlockRequest;
    resolve: () => void;
    reject: (reason: unknown) => void;
  };

  let pending = $state<Pending | null>(null);
  let identifier = $state('');
  let password = $state('');
  // Once the host asks for an emailed code we keep the typed password in memory and resubmit it
  // alongside the code — `createSession` takes all three at once.
  let needsTwoFactor = $state(false);
  let twoFactorToken = $state('');
  let submitting = $state(false);
  let error = $state<string | null>(null);
  let passwordField = $state<HTMLElement | null>(null);

  onMount(() =>
    registerPasswordUnlockPrompt(
      (request) =>
        new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
          identifier = request.handle ?? request.did;
          password = '';
          needsTwoFactor = false;
          twoFactorToken = '';
          submitting = false;
          error = null;
          pending = { request, resolve, reject };
          void tick().then(() => passwordField?.querySelector('input')?.focus());
        }),
    ),
  );

  /** Clear every credential this dialog held before it goes away. */
  function reset() {
    password = '';
    twoFactorToken = '';
    identifier = '';
    needsTwoFactor = false;
    error = null;
    submitting = false;
    pending = null;
  }

  function cancel() {
    const current = pending;
    reset();
    current?.reject({ code: UNLOCK_CANCELLED });

I'm refactoring the script to use the native `<dialog>` element with `showModal()` instead. I'll track the dialog element with a state variable and set up an effect that opens or closes it based on whether there's a pending operation. The tricky part is that the dialog rendering is currently guarded by a conditional, so I need to figure out how to handle that.

Actually, simpler approach: always render the dialog (it's hidden when closed anyway) and control it purely through `showModal()` and `close()`. The content inside stays guarded by the pending check. For the cancel and close handlers, I need to be careful about recursion—when the user presses Escape, the dialog fires `cancel` then `close`, so I'll prevent default on cancel if we're mid-flight, and check if pending is still set on close to handle unexpected closures. For focus, the native `showModal()` auto-focuses the first focusable element, but I can still use my tick-then-focus pattern to target the password field specifically.

I'm rethinking the structure: drop the manual window keydown handler since the dialog handles Escape natively, remove the redundant ARIA attributes (dialog already implies modal), and keep just the labelledby/describedby. For styling, I need to reset the dialog's default margin, border, and padding, then position it as a bottom sheet with transparent background and a styled backdrop using color-mix.

Writing dialog styles... Writing the dialog structure... Settling the first promise as cancelled when a second unlock request arrives, then storing the new request so only one dialog is active at a time. After that I need to handle the cleanup and write out the full file.

For focus management, I'm setting up an effect that opens the dialog when a pending request arrives and focuses the password input after the next tick, then closes it when the request is settled. The password field binding only exists in the non-2FA branch, which is fine.

When transitioning to 2FA, the dialog stays open but focus should shift to the code input field. I'll add a binding for the 2FA field and focus it after the error handler sets needsTwoFactor to true.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Make the unlock prompt a real modal and stop it stranding callers

Review follow-ups on the password unlock dialog.

Overlapping requests orphaned a caller. There is one prompt slot, and a second
`unlockIdentity` arriving while one was open overwrote `pending` outright — the
first caller's `resolve`/`reject` went with it and its `await` never settled.
Settle the outgoing request as a cancellation before the new one takes the slot.

Dismissal no longer depends on events that do not always fire. The dialog is now
a native `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`, so the browser owns focus
trapping, background inertness, and focus restoration — the previous `<div>` +
`role="dialog"` had none of those, and Tab reached the live controls behind the
scrim. But `showModal`'s *dismissal* signalling turned out to be the weak link:
verifying in the app WebView showed `close()` firing neither `cancel` nor
`close`, even for a freshly attached native listener. Relying on those events
would have reintroduced the stranded-caller bug through a different door, so
Escape is handled on `keydown` (universally delivered) with the default
suppressed; the `cancel`/`close` handlers stay as a no-op safety net where they
do fire.

Verified in the browser harness against the real component: `:modal` matches and
focusing a background button is refused; Escape closes, clears the credentials,
and returns to the locked screen with no error rendered; two overlapping
`unlockIdentity` calls settle the first as CANCELLED with the second prompt
usable; and the full screen-driven unlock still loads the app-password list.

The single-slot invariant lives in the component, which this repo has no Svelte
component-test setup to cover; the added `unlock.test.ts` case covers the half
that does live in the module — that a superseded prompt reaches the first caller
as a cancellation rather than hanging.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
